# watermarks-remover

<!-- logo: figlet -d .figlet -f cybermedium -w 120 "watermarks-remover" -->

[![CI](https://github.com/guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover)](https://github.com/guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover/releases)
[![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover)](https://github.com/guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover/stargazers)
[![Forks](https://img.shields.io/github/forks/guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover)](https://github.com/guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover/forks)

Agent skill + stdlib Python service to strip **multi-vendor AI provenance marks** from text and files — for privacy and hygiene on content **you own**. The skill is a thin client: it drives the machinery over HTTP, so the agent host needs no Python.

| Layer | Target | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | Invisible Unicode, exotic spaces, bidi, tag chars | Deterministic Python scripts |
| **B** | Statistical (token-sampling) text watermarks | Agent rewrite + optional `rewrite_text.py` hook |
| **Files** | C2PA / EXIF / XMP / doc props | PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, HEIC, BMP, GIF, TIFF, SVG, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, EPUB, ODT, HTML, Markdown, MP4/MOV/M4A/M4V, WAV, MP3, FLAC |

Vendors / ecosystems (class-level): **Claude**, **Gemini / SynthID-Text**, **OpenAI** provenance surfaces, **open-LLM** Kirchenbauer-style (green-list) and keyed-Gumbel / EXP (Aaronson) marks.

**Latest release:** [v0.7.0](https://github.com/guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover/releases/tag/v0.7.0)

Skill path: [`skills/remove-ai-marks/`](skills/remove-ai-marks/)  
Service path: [`service/`](service/)  
(migration: formerly `remove-claude-marks`; slash alias `/remove-claude-marks` still documented)

## Install (agent skill)

The skill ships **no code** — it calls the service over HTTP. Install the skill (markdown only) and start the service, then set `WATERMARKS_SERVICE_URL` if it is not `http://127.0.0.1:8765`.

In Claude Code, the fastest route is the bundled
[plugin marketplace](#claude-code-plugin-marketplace) — no clone, and it updates
in place. Everywhere else, one installer covers every supported host
(Python 3.10+ stdlib, no dependencies):

```bash
python3 install_skill.py --skill remove-ai-marks --target claude-code

deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.content: # DeepSeek Harness English | [中文](README.zh.md) DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) is an open-source agent harness developed by [DeepSeek AI](https://deepseek.com). It is built on an **everything-is-a-plugin** architecture and powered by [Cordis](https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis), whose design is described in [_A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability_](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25512). Documentation: [https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/) ## Developer preview DeepSeek Harness is in _developer preview_ and iterating rapidly. **THERE WILL BE COMPATIBILITY-BREAKING CHANGES.** Review the [safety notice](SAFETY.md) before running the project. ## Run ### Run from `npm` Install `Node.js`, then run: ```sh npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web ``` The command starts the Web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:3080` by default and opens it in the default browser for a local launch. An SSH launch only prints the host URL because the SSH client or editor owns the local forwarded address. Pass `--no-open` to run the server without opening a browser. See [Web UI guide](docs/user/guide/index.md). ### Run from source To run from a repository checkout: ```sh git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.git cd deepseek-harness pnpm install pnpm run build pnpm dsh web ``` `pnpm run build` prepares the repository artifacts. `pnpm dsh web` uses those built artifacts without rebuilding. ## Community and support - Submit feedback or bug reports through [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions). - Add the [`dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) topic to your plugin repository for discoverability. - Join DeepSeek Harness Discord community. ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Development Start with the [development guide](docs/development.md) and [architecture documentation](docs/architecture.md). `pnpm run dev:web` builds, serves, and rebuilds client bundles on source edits in one terminal, and `make help` lists the matching Make targets for Web and Desktop; the guide's application commands section owns the full table. For agents, follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). ## Citation ```bibtex @misc{deepseek-harness2026, title={DeepSeek Harness: Everything is a Plugin}, author={DeepSeek-AI}, year={2026}, publisher={GitHub}, howpublished={\url{https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness}}, } ``` ## License [MIT](LICENSE) Third-party dependencies and their licenses are disclosed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

browser-use/jev-ultrafast.content: > [!NOTE] > **Jev Ultrafast is now ultrafast mode in [Browser Use](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use).** Same idea, built in: the agent acts on numbered page elements. Browser Use also handles long multi-step tasks. > > Python: `pip install browser-use`, then `Agent(task, mode='ultrafast')` (already the default on the `bu-fast` and `bu-ultrafast` models). Hosted: the `bu-ultrafast` model in Browser Use Cloud. > > This repo stays up as the original Browser Use × TypeSafe experiment. # Jev Ultrafast ⚡ > [!IMPORTANT] > **BU Ultrafast, Browser Use Cloud's own hosted agent, is live on every plan.** Set `model: "bu-ultrafast"` to use it. > **[Learn more](https://browser-use.com/ultrafast?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=jev-ultrafast)** · **[Open Browser Use Cloud](https://cloud.browser-use.com?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=jev-ultrafast)** **A browser agent with a dynamic, indexed action space.** Give it one goal. [TypeSafe's Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction) picks an operation and an element. A small LLM writes text only when the operation is `TYPE_TEXT`. **Zürich → London on Google Flights in 7.1 seconds.** One natural-language goal, actual text generation, and loading waits included. [Watch the MP4](docs/demo.mp4) · [Measurements](docs/performance.md) · [Read the loop](jev_ultrafast/agent.py) ## The action space Every observation produces a new element table: ```text [1] button Change ticket type · Round trip [2] combobox Where from? · San Francisco [3] combobox Where to? · empty [4] textbox Departure · empty ... ``` The operations are `CLICK`, `TYPE_TEXT`, `SELECT`, `SCROLL_UP`, `SCROLL_DOWN`, `WAIT`, `DONE`, and `BLOCKED`. Only supported operations and targets are offered. ```text one TypeSafe request ┌───────────────────────────┐ page → element table → operation │ │ click_target │ │ type_text_target │ │ select_target, if present │ └─────────────┬─────────────┘ use the matching target │ CLICK [7] ─────┤──→ browser TYPE_TEXT [3] ─────┘ ↓ small LLM → text → browser ``` Target questions are speculative. If the operation is `CLICK`, only `click_target` can execute. Two decisions, **one network round trip**. Each target head contains only compatible elements. # Compositor

Adobe Photoshop costs too much and tools like GIMP don’t feel familiar enough for me to stay in flow. That’s why I built Compositor.

The goal was to create a full-featured image editor that is completely free and open source. I used to use Photoshop for compositing and post-processing, so Compositor is built around that workflow - with the tools needed to create a pixel-perfect final image.

Because it’s open source, you can download the Xcode project and add, remove, or modify any feature to fit your workflow.

## Installation

### Download
Get Compositor from [robbietilton.com/compositor](https://robbietilton.com/compositor), or download the latest release directly from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/robbietilton/Compositor/releases/latest).

### Homebrew

```sh
brew install --cask robbietilton-compositor
```

## Features

### Layers
- Layers and folders, with opacity and Photoshop's full set of blend modes in its order — a folder's opacity dims everything inside it
- Layer masks: paint, fill, invert, blur and feather them anywhere on the canvas, past the layer's own pixels; link or unlink them to transform a mask on its own
- Clipping masks and folder masks
- Adjustment layers: Hue/Saturation, Levels, Curves, Exposure, Gradient Map, Grain, Black & White, Color Balance, Invert, and filter layers: Gaussian Blur, Motion Blur, Progressive Blur, Sharpen, Reduce Noise, Noise, Vignette, Bloom / Glow, RGB Split, Lens Effects and Tonal Contrast
- Layer effects: Stroke, Drop Shadow, Color Overlay, Inner Shadow, Outer Glow and Inner Glow, rendered on the GPU and editable at any time
- Merge Down, Merge Layers and Merge Group (⌘E)
- Duplicate, rename inline, reorder and nest by drag and drop; Option-drag to duplicate; a right-click menu in the Layers panel
- Copy and paste whole layers and folders (⌘C/⌘V with no selection), within a project or between projects, or drag them between projects

### Transform
- Non-destructive move, scale, rotate and flip — images keep their full resolution however small you make them
- Free distort (⌘-drag a handle), with Shift to lock to an axis
- Transform several layers, or a whole folder, together
- Snapping to canvas and layer edges and centers, with guides
- Distances (View › Show › Distances): pixel gaps to the canvas edges and nearby layers while moving a layer, and to the layer under the pointer with ⌘ held
- Exact values for position, size, scale and angle, stepped with the arrow keys
- Flip Layer and Flip Canvas, horizontal and vertical
- Align and Distribute layers to each other, the selection or the canvas, from the Move tool's bar or the Layer menu

### Selections
- Rectangle and Ellipse Marquee, Freehand and Polygonal Lasso, and the Magic tool — Wand selects by color, Object traces whatever you click (Tab switches)
- Select Subject, and Expand, Contract and Feather on any selection
- Add to and subtract from selections, move the outline, or move and duplicate the pixels inside
- Load a lay…

# Readme

This repository contains mathematical manuscripts and supporting proof artifacts produced by an unnamed internal OpenAI model. 

As part of model development, we evaluate our models on open research problems. We expanded these evaluations after performance on our existing mathematical evaluations saturated. Some outputs build upon earlier results produced by the models.

This collection includes results at different stages of verification. Not all have accompanying Lean formalizations. We will continue to update this repository with Lean formalizations as we obtain them. 

Some of the unformalized results could have issues. We will endeavor to fix any such issues quickly.
We are also exploring community-hosted repositories for these materials. 

In our view, these manuscripts are best understood as a form of raw research data, rather than polished academic papers. We defer to the math community completely on matters of credit, precedence, and concurrent work.

## Navigating the collection

The current catalogue contains 721 manuscripts organized into 373 families. A family groups related papers, which may include a principal result, companion arguments, consequences, or alternative proofs. Each family is classified by mathematical discipline.

- Start with the [overview](overview.pdf) for descriptions of the families.
- Use the [manuscript map](CONTENTS.md) to find individual papers and their supporting materials.
- The [`preprints/`](preprints/) directory contains PDFs, source files, and manuscript-specific citation and build instructions.
- The [Lean library](lean/README.md) and [formalization catalogue](lean/formalization.yaml) describe the available formal proofs, their associated papers, and verification configurations. See the [Comparator instructions](lean/ComparatorChallenges/README.md) for additional checking instructions. The repository has ~42% top-line results formalized.
- Updates to the repo are described in the [history](history.md).

### Reasoning summaries

We are also releasing abridged summaries of the model's reasoning, covering the following results:

# DeepInfer

DeepInfer is the high-performance inference framework that powers DeepSeek's large-scale production services. This open-source release provides offline inference with the core features needed for serving at scale.

Supported models:

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

Supported features:

- Optimized kernels, model and sampler runtime
- Parallelism: Attention DP / balanced CP, MoE EP + EPLB
- DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification
- SWA bounded replay
- Asynchronous scheduling (zero-overhead batch scheduler)
- Batch-invariant inference
- Deterministic sampling
- Structured outputs

<details>
<summary>Feature details and configuration</summary>

- **Optimized kernels:** [FlashMLA](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/FlashMLA), [DeepGEMM](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM), [DeepEP](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP), [TileKernels](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/TileKernels), [DeepSelect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect), and custom [TileLang kernels](deepinfer/model_executor/layers/tilelang_ops).
- **DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification:** accelerate decoding with draft tokens and use confidence estimates to schedule verification. Set `DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=1`; `DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE` controls the maximum draft length (default: 5).
- **Decoder SWA bounded replay:** reduce decoder prefill work by replaying only a bounded suffix. Set `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_TRUNCATION_MODE=compact` and `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_KEEP_TOKENS=140` for the default V4.1 settings; the retained suffix must cover the SWA window plus the maximum backtracking length.
- **Asynchronous scheduling:** overlap CPU batch scheduling with device execution. Enabled by default.
- **Batch-invariant inference:** keep model results identical across different batch compositions. Enable with `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (NVIDIA only).
- **Deterministic sampling:** produce identical outputs for identical input tokens and sampling parameters. Set `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=0` and pass a fixed `seq_seed` to `SamplingParams` (NVIDIA only).
- **Structured outputs:** constrain generation to a regex, JSON schema, or EBNF grammar. Pass `so_args={"schema_type": ..., "schema": ...}` to `SamplingParams`; see [examples](examples/_structured_output.py).

</details>

Supported hardware:

- NVIDIA SM100 GPUs
- Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs

Required for a complete inference service (not included in this release):

- A KV cache system
- VE/Prefill/Decode disaggregation (most required engine functionality is already implemented)
- Load balancing across data-parallel replicas for both prefill and decode

- Linux
- GCC >= 13.0
- Python 3.12
- CUDA 13 (NVIDIA only)
- CANN 9.2 (Ascend only)

google-research/harness2.content:
Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World

A **harness** is the system around a model that enables it to act as an agent: prompts, tools, memory, skills, orchestration, and more. **Harnessing** is the process of optimizing that system. Harness² is a plug-and-play framework for **recursive agent harnessing** in an open world, where agents encounter tasks unseen during harness design. It connects two levels of recursion while keeping model weights fixed: * **Task-level recursion** refines the execution harness for the current task through a contrastive **Propose–Probe–Compose** step: propose edits, probe their effects on the same task, and compose a refined harness from behavioral contrasts between executions, without ground-truth feedback. * **Harnessing-level recursion** updates a persistent *improvement harness* with adopted harnesses and evidence-supported lessons from each task to guide future refinement.

Across three professional benchmarks and four model–harness configurations, a single Harness² step improves GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base harnesses, with gains of up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 points on JobBench, and 11.8 percentage points on LAB's partial pass rate. Increasing the task-level recursion budget brings further gains. The release supports **parallel and sequential recursion**, **OpenCode and Codex executors**, and **JobBench, LAB, and WorkBuddy-Bench**. ## Video overview https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76b10548-b14b-4c8f…

training and unquantized inference uses. The same silicon sold as an RTX A-series
or professional card runs at full rate. `gpu_unlock` removes that cap at boot,
before the stock NVIDIA driver loads. No patched driver, no VBIOS flash, nothing
to redo when NVIDIA releases a new driver.

---

## Supported GPUs

| Generation                | Cards                                                                                                                  | Status                    |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| **Ampere** (RTX 30)       | RTX 3050, 3060, 3060 Ti, 3070, 3070 Ti, 3080, 3080 Ti, 3090, 3090 Ti, plus RTX 3070/3080 Laptop GPUs                   | Stable, 100+ user reports |
| **Ada Lovelace** (RTX 40) | RTX 4060, 4060 Ti, 4070, 4070 SUPER, 4070 Ti, 4070 Ti SUPER, 4080, 4080 SUPER, 4090, 4090 D, RTX 4050/4060 Laptop GPUs | Experimental              |
| **Turing** (RTX 20)       | RTX 2060, 2060 SUPER, 2070, 2070 SUPER, 2080, 2080 SUPER, 2080 Ti, Titan RTX                                           | Experimental              |
| Blackwell (RTX 50)        |                                                                                                                        | Not supported             |

Laptops only stay unlocked if the dedicated GPU is never fully powered off.  
Many laptops power it down when idle, which silently resets the unlock. Turning  
off runtime power management with `options nvidia NVreg_DynamicPowerManagement=0x00`
in `/etc/modprobe.d/` helps on some models, but expect mixed results.

The exact PCI device IDs are in [`kernel/gpu_unlock/recipes.c`](kernel/gpu_unlock/recipes.c).
Linux only. For Windows see the [FAQ](#faq).

aschmelyun/print-my-profile-pic.content: # print-my-profile-pic Star this repo to have your GitHub profile picture framed, printed out on my receipt printer, and stuck to my wall. That's it! > [!TIP] > If you give a one-time [sponsorship](https://github.com/sponsors/aschmelyun?frequency=one-time&sponsor=aschmelyun) of any amount beforehand, your profile picture will be printed in a **special frame**. ## How's it work? GitHub allows you to create webhooks for specific events on your repos, I've set one up for [starring](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#star) this project. When that happens, a payload is POSTed to a [Cloudflare tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/) domain, which leads to a PHP script running on a Raspberry Pi that's sitting on my desk. From the inbound request, you can gleen info about the person who starred the repo, like their display name and avatar URL. The script takes their profile picture, renders it behind a cut-out of a photo frame, and then adds some other info I thought should be included in each receipt. The RPi is connected to an Epson TM-T88IV thermal receipt printer via USB, and the PHP script uses my go-to [escpos-php](https://github.com/mike42/escpos-php) library to format the receipt data and send it off to the printer. ## But why? It sounded fun when my friend [Sam](https://x.com/samwhoo) mentioned it. That's pretty much it! ## What now? I'll periodically update this README with a picture of the pinboard I've dubbed the "Hall of Frame" as pictures get added to it. Want to add a new frame? Send in a PR!

# TotK Recomp

**TotK Recomp** is a static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom* (Nintendo Switch, 2023) into a native Windows x86-64 application ([docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of *Tears of the Kingdom*, dumped from your own console: the base game and the 1.2.1 or 1.4.3 update. Instructions for obtaining those files will not be provided.
>
> The game is built from your files on your machine, so the result contains the game. It is for your own use. Do not share it.

## Status

Early development. The game is playable on Windows; visual bugs and crashes are still expected.

Report problems as issues, following [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Features

- Native code, not emulation
- Game updates 1.2.1 and 1.4.3, with saves that carry over between them
- 60 fps by default; up to 144 fps or the monitor's refresh rate (experimental)
- Custom resolutions (1080p, 2k...), supersampling and AMD FSR 1 upscaling
- In-game settings menu (F1) and performance overlay (F10)
- Keyboard, mouse and gamepad with remapping, rumble and gyro
- Shaders prepared at install instead of during play

## Planned

- Linux and the Steam Deck
- Mods made for emulators: unpack a mod into a `mods` folder
- Custom aspect ratios, including ultrawide
- VRR

## Installing

Requirements: Windows 10 or later, an x86-64 CPU with AVX2, a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 and `VK_EXT_external_memory_host`, about 36 GiB free during setup (20 GiB after).

1. Download `TotK-Setup-<version>-windows.zip` from [Releases](../../releases/latest) and unpack it.
2. Start `TotK-Setup.exe`. If SmartScreen warns about an unsigned app, choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
3. Pick your game files, the language and an install folder, and press *Start*. The setup builds the game once.
4. Play `totk.exe` from the install folder.

To update, run a newer `TotK-Setup.exe` on the same folder; saves and settings are kept. Settings are in the in-game menu and in `totk.ini` ([totk.ini.example](totk.ini.example) lists every key). Controls: [docs/controls.md](docs/controls.md).

TotK Recomp builds on the projects below. What was taken from each, with its license, is listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

# Subvox

A macOS prototype that tests whether AirPods Pro head-motion data (`CMHeadphoneMotionManager`) carries enough information to turn **silently mouthed words into text**.

It doesn't use a language model. It's a small-vocabulary template recognizer plus a statistical test that tells you whether the signal is real.

## Build & run

```sh
brew install xcodegen   # once
xcodegen generate
open Subvox.xcodeproj   # ⌘R
```

Or from the command line:

```sh
xcodebuild -project Subvox.xcodeproj -scheme Subvox -derivedDataPath build -allowProvisioningUpdates build
open build/Build/Products/Debug/Subvox.app
xcodebuild -project Subvox.xcodeproj -scheme Subvox -derivedDataPath build test
```

Requires macOS 14+, AirPods Pro or another headphone that supports head tracking, connected as the Mac's audio output. On first launch, grant **Motion**. The mic and speech prompts only appear when you start the mic.

## Screens

| Screen | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Sensors** | Live plots of user acceleration, rotation rate and attitude, the measured sample rate, a mic input picker and level meter, and a recorder for experiment sessions. |
| **Train** | Pick a word, hold **Space**, mouth it, release. Each take is stored as a template. **Evaluate** runs leave-one-out classification and a 500× label-permutation test, then shows accuracy against chance, a p-value and a confusion matrix. The feature checkboxes (acceleration / rotation / attitude) let you test which channels carry the signal. |
| **Decode** | The motion-to-text screen. Hold Space, or use auto-detect after calibrating the noise floor. Each segment is DTW-matched against your templates and added to the transcript. A live mic transcript runs alongside it for comparison. |

## How decoding works

1. **Segmentation** (`CaptureController`). Space-hold, or an energy trigger above a calibrated noise floor with pre-roll and hangover.
2. **Features** (`MotionFeatures`). Per frame: user acceleration (3), rotation rate (3), and attitude change since the start of the segment (3). Each channel is mean-centered, and quiet lead-in and lead-out frames are trimmed.
3. **Matching** (`DTW`, `TemplateClassifier`). Each channel is z-scaled across the training set. Matching is 1-nearest-neighbour per word, using dynamic time warping with a Sakoe–Chiba band. A segment is rejected if the best distance is above *max distance* or the margin to the runner-up is below *min confidence*.
4. **Is it real?** (`Evaluation`). The leave-one-out accuracy is compared with the same procedure run on shuffled labels. If p < 0.05, the motion stream distinguishes your words better than chance.

## Experiment protocol

Use **Record Session** in the toolbar or on the Sensors screen. Recordings go to `~/Documents/Subvox/Sessions/<timestamp>-<condition>/`:

- `motion.csv`: every motion sample. `t` is seconds from session start.
- `audio.caf`: microphone audio, if the mic is running.
- `events.csv`: every Space-held segment, with its label or pr…

# DrewLevin Detector

A League of Legends match-history tool with a sense of humor. Enter a Riot ID,
get a Drew Index, and open **THE RECEIPTS** to inspect the matches behind each
detected change.

Live site: [drewed.lol](https://drewed.lol/)

## What it does

- Reviews every Solo/Duo and Flex match returned for the current year and the
  previous two years, with paginated history requests.
- Compares Flash placement, item slots, rune pages, champion and role habits,
  and sustained performance changes across that history.
- Keeps Solo/Duo and Flex performance comparisons separate while comparing
  mechanical habits across both queues.
- Shows dated evidence, baseline comparisons, match IDs, participant details,
  and complete rune pages in dialogs.
- Provides a scan queue, progress updates, cached match details, and local game
  assets.

Supported platforms: **NA1, BR1, LA1, LA2, EUW1, EUN1, TR1**.

The Drew Index is a heuristic score derived from the available match history.
Coverage depends on the matches the upstream services still return. OP.GG and
Rewind can supplement historical rank labels or totals; those aggregates do
not supply the individual matches used as evidence.

## Run locally

Requirements: Node.js **22.13 or newer**, npm, and one
[Riot API key](https://developer.riotgames.com/).

```sh
npm ci
```

Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in the single server-side variable:

```dotenv
RIOT_API_KEY=
```

```sh
npm run dev
```

Open [localhost:5173](http://localhost:5173). The key is used only by server-side
API routes. Keep `.env.local` private; Git and Docker builds exclude it.
Restart the application after replacing the token.

For UI previews without Riot requests, use `/?preview=low` or `/?preview=queue`.

## API requests and pacing

All Riot calls go through `lib/riot.ts` and use **one** `RIOT_API_KEY`. Requests
to each routing host share a queue, with a 1.3-second minimum interval between
starts. A 429 response pauses that queue according to `Retry-After`. Temporary
network and server failures receive up to three attempts; a rejected token
returns an error.

The application processes one account scan at a time per running instance.
Analysis results are cached in memory for a short time, and match details are
cached in memory for up to 24 hours. Queue and cache ownership assume a single
application instance. The KV binding stores the counter and progress updates.

## Checks

```sh
npm test
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm run check:secrets
npm run build
```

Tests use deterministic upstream responses and a virtual clock. They do not
need an API key or call Riot. The secret check scans Git's tracked and untracked
publishable files without printing matched secret values.

## Docker

Create `.env.local` as above, then run:

```sh
docker compose -f compose.production.yml up -d --build
```

The service listens on `127.0.0.1:4173`. Compose mounts the environment file as a
runtime secret and uses the `detector-state` volume …

# RAN Sentinel

An AI co-engineer for mobile networks, built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon.

RAN Sentinel watches a cluster of LTE cells in Seattle, WA (US bands B66, B2 and B71) and spots a degrading cell. Muse Spark agents investigate it with read-only tools and propose a fix. Fixed safety rules and a digital twin check that fix before anyone sees it. The recommendation then goes to the right department. When a configuration change is approved, it is sent as an Open M-Plane change package with automatic rollback, and the cell is watched until it recovers. Customers of the fictional operator **Northstar Connect** see only confirmed, plain-language updates.

Everything runs on a **simulated** network. Nothing here connects to a real operator.

**New since 2026-10-30:** a verified investigation built on the patterns in Meta's
[legal-agent workshop](https://github.com/meta-models/legal-agent-workshop). Every diagnosis passes a verifier the agents cannot skip.
The agent pauses to ask a field engineer when the data cannot settle a cause. It keeps a living plan, works one tool per turn and
resumes from its last step after an API failure, and an engineer signs off the root cause
([details](docs/VERIFIED_INVESTIGATION.md)). Customers also get a hands-free **voice agent** that operates the app

**Hackathon entry:** Indie track, theme "Build for Your World". The submission summary is in [SUBMISSION.md](SUBMISSION.md), the 3-minute demo script is in [DEMO.md](DEMO.md), and the code is MIT-licensed ([LICENSE](LICENSE)).

# Span

Span implements a branch relaxing assembler in Isabelle/HOL, with proofs of termination, minimum layout size and execution correspondence for a bytecode machine with signed 8-bit and 16-bit relative branches

[![](media/demo.gif)](media/demo.mp4)

## Correctness

An overflowing short branch must be wide in every valid assignment. [Relaxation](Relax.thy) computes the least widening set terminating on the number of remaining short branches. A final range check decides whether any valid layout exists

[Encoding](Encoding.thy) proves byte bounds and decoder inversion and [Execution correspondence](Machine.thy) relates source execution `S` and bytecode execution `B` through relocation `R` for every fuel bound (including suspended states)

![](media/correspondence.svg)

Minimality assumes fixed instruction order and excludes alignment directives while the machine uses a natural valued accumulator and biased little endian branch payloads. The execution theorem starts from resolved instructions and excludes the SML compiler, runtime and OS I/O

# unslop

Created by Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)), who started the [Unslopping series](https://x.com/heydamir/status/2115063463063998736) on X.

![A vibecoded dashboard unslopping itself, frame by frame](skills/unslop/references/refs/story-dashboard-frames.webp)

unslop is a skill for Claude Code, Codex and Google Antigravity that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

## Install

For Claude Code, install it as a plugin. Run this in a terminal to get it in every project:

```bash
claude plugin install unslop --marketplace heydamir/unslop
```

On an older Claude Code without `--marketplace`, the same in two steps:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add heydamir/unslop
claude plugin install unslop@heydamir
```

To get it in a single project only, run the install from that project's root folder, the one you start Claude Code in, and add `--scope local`. To turn it on for everyone who works in the project, add `--scope project` instead and commit `.claude/settings.json`. Each teammate then runs this once in their own copy of the project:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add heydamir/unslop
claude plugin install unslop@heydamir --scope project
```

Then start a new Claude Code session, or run `/reload-plugins` in one that is already open.

To update, run `claude plugin update unslop@heydamir`, or turn on auto-update for the heydamir marketplace under Marketplaces in `/plugin`.

If you copied unslop into `~/.claude/skills/` or a project's `.claude/skills/` before, delete that copy, or `/unslop` keeps running it instead of the plugin.

For Codex, ask it to install the skill straight from this repo.

```
$skill-installer install https://github.com/heydamir/unslop/tree/main/skills/unslop
```

Or copy it by hand into `~/.agents/skills/`, or into `.agents/skills/` inside a single project.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.agents/skills/
```

For Google Antigravity, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.gemini/config/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.gemini/config/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.agents/skills/` inside that project instead.

To snapshot a live site or create a story video, install Playwright and its Chromium browser from the project directory where you run the skill:

```bash
npm install -D playwright
npx playwright install chromium
```

Story videos also require ffmpeg installed and available…

lexifina/global-law.content:
# Git for Global Law

**The world's law in one git history. Every word traced to the law that wrote it for any country and any date.**

An expansion of the same for the US Code, [#1 on Hacker News (28/10/26)](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50268380).
Semantic, searchable law on a global scale.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f24f3411-24d9-416a-8c45-9cebc817c64e

**Free to use: [CC0](LICENSE.md).** Fork it, build on it, ship it in a product: no permission or credit needed. The law text
sits in each country's repository, under that repository's own terms.

The law of many jurisdictions as one git history. Each jurisdiction's law is its own repository, where every commit
is one law taking effect, written by that law. This repository arranges those repositories by jurisdiction and
interleaves their histories in the order the changes took force, so a single commit here is the state of all of them on
one day.

```
global-law/
├── manifest.json            every corpus: path, source repo, coverage, which trailer holds the in-force date
├── jurisdiction.json        the world, and its children: 193 UN members, other territories with their own ISO code, and the EU
├── germany/                 Germany (ISO code DE in its jurisdiction.json)
│   ├── SOURCES.md           where German law can be read, with what each source offers
│   └── bund/                federal law
│       └── acts/            submodule: the Grundgesetz since 1949 (grundgesetz/), every other federal act since 2019
├── estonia/                 Estonia
│   └── national/acts/       submodule: Estonia's law history, from its corpus.json
├── france/                  France: jurisdiction.json and SOURCES.md, no history yet
└── …                        every other country, the same way
```

Each country's law lives in its own repository, `lexifina/<country>-law`, which says where it belongs here in a
`corpus.json` at its root. A country whose repository still holds only its sources (no law yet) has a folder with its
`jurisdiction.json` and `SOURCES.md`, and no submodule: only real law is pinned. Laws adopted but not yet in force stay
on each corpus's future branch; `main` here holds only what is in force by the build date.

Corpora differ widely in reach. Some hold a country's whole statute book (Czechia, Spain, Switzerland, Georgia, Malta);
others hold a few acts, or a sample: the US corpus is nine titles of the United States Code, and the UK corpus is the
special educational needs law. `manifest.json` gives each corpus's `coverage`, and `history` says how its past is known:
`in-force` (dated official versions), `replayed` (rebuilt by applying each amending act; its `verification` says which
dates were checked) or `current-only` (today's text only).

## Using it from an AI model (MCP)

# Openjutsu

An open-source, Genjutsu-style character and object swap for video. Drop a video and a character photo, press **Generate**, and the main person in the video is replaced by your character. Or change their hair or clothes, remove something, or put them somewhere else. The camera, cuts, motion and soundtrack stay. Everything runs on open weights on your own GPU: MiniMax H3 for the video, SAM 3.1 to track people, and Qwen3-VL 8B to describe the pictures and shots.

The app is a small Next.js front end over a ComfyUI workflow. It uses [`@comfyorg/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@comfyorg/sdk), following Comfy's [comfy-reshoot](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-reshoot) reference app.

| --- | --- |
| ![Two people swapped, each from their own photo](docs/media/advanced_swap.jpg) | ![Sunglasses painted onto a person's eyes](docs/media/object_swap.jpg) |
| **From picture: a new look and place from one picture** | **Post-processing: fix faces** |
| ![A video frame and a picture combined into a posed picture, then a video](docs/media/from_picture.jpg) | ![A small face redrawn at close-up size](docs/media/fix_faces.jpg) |

**From picture → Relight: new light in the same pass**

![A video frame and a picture combined into a posed picture under golden backlight, then a video that keeps the light, with the seventeen light looks below](docs/media/relight.jpg)

## First visit: visual describer

The welcome page lets you choose the vision-language model that describes pictures and video frames and writes prompts. Qwen3-VL 8B INT8 remains the default; Qwen3-VL 4B FP8 and Gemma 4 E2B INT8 are smaller alternatives. Install a compatible single-file model including its vision weights in `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders`, then press **Refresh models**. Other installed models can be selected if they support image/video input and text generation through ComfyUI's CLIPLoader and Generate Text nodes. Text-only models and files requiring a different loader are unsuitable.

Choose according to available VRAM and leave room for image/video context and working memory; file size is not a VRAM requirement, and H3 generation has separate memory needs. Your selection is saved in this browser and used for swaps, prompt descriptions and **Find people**. Reopen **Welcome & models** to change it, or use **Visual describer** under Model components. Alternative describers may change prompt quality and person matching. **Set up later** opens the editor; generation still checks the required files. The separate H3 text encoder remains unchanged.

## Modes

- **Simple motion transfer**: available. One character replaces the main person (the one who fills the most of the frame). Runs `workflows/simple.api.json`, exported from `H3 One-Click Single Swap (DMAD 6 step).json`.

# Setup

1. Clone the repo:
   git clone https://github.com/SPIRAME/Emudhroll && cd Emudhroll
2. Install requirements:
   pip install -r requirements.txt
3. Run the proxy:
   python main.py
4. Permanent unenrollment mode:
   python main.py --permanent
5. Re-enroll:
   python main.py --enroll

The proxy listens on port 8080.

## Chromebook setup (normal unenroll)

1. Powerwash the Chromebook.
2. On the OOBE screen, connect to Wi-Fi and open its proxy settings. (it is necessary to do it on the welcome as revocation will occur otherwise if not done fast enough)
3. Set to Manual proxy configuration.
4. Enable Use the same proxy for all protocols.
5. Enter your computer's IP and port 8080.
6. Continue through OOBE and it should unenrolol

## Permanent unenrollment (--permanent)

1. Start the proxy: python main.py --permanent
2. Go through OOBE on the Chromebook.
3. When prompted, powerwash the device then press y.
4. On powerwash, It will successfully unenrollol

## Re-enroll (--enroll)

1. Run: python main.py --enroll
2. Enter the stable device secret (hex) when prompted (this is obtained via entering devmode and running vpd -l as root in vt2)
3. On powerwash, it will successfully reenroll

# dsh-superagent

> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat it as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style and engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own environment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*. Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.

dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.

## Setup

Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:

> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is what it follows.

## Documentation

Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it.

- [000 Philosophy](docs/000-philosophy.md)
- [001 Domain model](docs/001-domain.md)
- [002 Authorization](docs/002-authorization.md)
- [003 Execution](docs/003-execution.md)
- [004 Prompts](docs/004-prompts.md)
- [005 Panel](docs/005-panel.md)
- [006 Deployment](docs/006-deployment.md): manual setup, configuration, upgrades and troubleshooting
- [007 Architecture](docs/007-architecture.md)
- [008 Cookbook](docs/008-cookbook.md): adding a Source

## Development

`pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build.

Arjun-Ingole/hop.content:
Install Linux next to Windows without a USB stick.

## What it is hop is a single Windows app that installs Linux alongside Windows. Pick a system, choose a drive, drag to choose how much space it gets, and click Install. There's no USB stick to find and nothing to install first. ## What it does - **Downloads from official sources.** It gets the ISO from the project's own server and verifies its checksum where the project publishes one. You can also use an ISO you already have. - **Makes room safely.** It checks your PC first, and nothing on the disk changes until those checks pass. - **Goes where there's room.** Shrink C: or another drive, use free space, or use a second disk inside the PC. If C: is full, hop suggests a drive that isn't, and the download can go elsewhere too. - **Tells you what to click.** It lists the exact choices to make in the Linux installer. - **Gets you unstuck.** If the PC goes back to Windows, reopening hop explains why and can restart into the BIOS. - **Cleans up after itself.** Undo gives the space back to the drive it came from, and it can also remove another Linux already on the drive. - **Can replace Windows entirely, for the systems where hop has seen it work:** Ubuntu, Xubuntu, Ubuntu Budgie, Ubuntu Cinnamon, Edubuntu, Ubuntu Studio, Zorin OS, Fedora Workstation, Ultramarine, elementary OS, Debian, Arch and Omarchy. It's a separate choice with its own warning, and you have to type ERASE. hop only makes the installer, which copies itself to memory so it can erase the disk it started from when you tell it to. It needs more memory than the ISO's size, and it's only offered for systems where hop has seen it erase a disk and start again afterwards. **Systems:** elementary OS, Ubuntu and its flavours (Budgie, Xubuntu, Lubuntu, Cinnamon, Unity, Edubuntu, Studio), Linux Mint, Pop!_OS, Zorin OS, Debian, Fedora Workstation, Ultramarine, CachyOS, Arch Linux and Omarchy. Other Ubuntu-based ISOs should work too, if you choose the file yourself. Kubuntu isn't supported, because its ISO has a file too big for FAT32. CachyOS, Arch, Omarchy and Pop!_OS need Secure Boot off. Omarchy also needs BitLocker fully off on its disk, not paused, and hop refuses until it is. hop won't turn it off for you. **Needs:** Windows 10 (1803 or newer) or 11, on a UEFI PC with a GPT disk, which is nearly every PC sold with them. Linux has to go on a disk inside the PC, not a USB drive. ## How it works A USB installer is just a FAT32 drive with the ISO's files on it. hop makes the same thing on you…

# nv-uefi-unlocker

[中文](README.md) | [English](README.en.md)

**你的 GeForce 正以半速跑 AI——这个工具在驱动加载前把它修复。**

[![version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.1.8-brightgreen)](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/releases/latest)

[![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-UEFI%20%E9%A2%84%E9%A9%B1%E5%8A%A8%20%7C%20Win%20%2F%20Linux%20%2F%20Hackintosh-blue)](docs/faq.md)

**实测 FP16 / BF16 / TF32 张量吞吐最高约 2.6× · FP8 最高约 1.9× · 图像 / 视频生成 +14–75% · DirectML 推理算子最高 +94% · 无 VBIOS 刷写，断电即复原**（逐卡数据见[兼容性矩阵](docs/compatibility.md)；增益受功耗墙与精度路径制约）

GTX 16 + RTX 20 + RTX 30 + RTX 40 系列通用的 UEFI 预驱动 NVIDIA GPU 解锁工具。

解开 NVIDIA 显卡的 Tensor 计算性能限制。从 U 盘启动，解锁后自动进入 Windows 或 Linux 或任意操作系统，无需刷写 VBIOS；断电后恢复原状。

[观看项目宣传片 ↗](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1d6xN66ECM/)

## 兼容性速览

| 系列 | 支持情况 |
| --- | --- |
| GTX 16 · Turing | 理论兼容，欢迎实机验证 |
| RTX 20 · Turing | 全系兼容；部分型号有已知问题，见完整矩阵 |
| RTX 30 · Ampere GA10x | 全系兼容，支持笔记本与台式 |
| RTX 40 · Ada | 全系兼容，支持笔记本与台式 |
| Pascal 及更早 / GA100 / RTX 50 | 不支持 |

[完整兼容性矩阵与逐卡实测](docs/compatibility.md) · [常见问题](docs/faq.md)

## 开始使用

### 1. 获取工具并检查前置条件

从 [Releases](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/releases) 下载并解压发布包。发布包不附带 NVIDIA 固件，制盘脚本会自动下载指定版本并校验、生成所需文件。

准备一个 FAT32 U 盘，先备份其中的文件。目标机器须使用 UEFI 启动，关闭 Secure Boot，或为 EFI 自签并信任证书。笔记本优先使用独显直连，从系统选择“重启”后进入一次性启动菜单。

**Turing 用户先在目标 Windows 的管理员 PowerShell 运行一次，再重启：**

```powershell
.\enable-turing-unlock.ps1
```

重启后确认 GSP 固件已运行，再制作 U 盘。Linux Turing 目标同样需要 GSP-RM；详见 [GSP 前置说明](docs/faq.md#turing)。Linux 用户还应检查 [RTD3](docs/faq.md#linux)，避免进入系统后掉电丢失解锁。

### 2. 制作启动 U 盘

在**目标机**（要解锁的机器）的解压目录直接运行：脚本自动识别本机显卡代际，只生成并下载对应固件。

Windows PowerShell：

```powershell
.\make-usbroot.ps1
```

Linux / WSL / Git Bash：

```bash
bash make-usbroot.sh
```

在另一台机器上制作时显式指定代际：40 系 `-Family 40`，30 系 `30`，20 / 16 系 `20`。`-Family all` 把三代固件全部打进同一张 U 盘（一条命令即可服务多种卡）。

Windows 需要 PowerShell 5+；Linux 版需要 glibc ≥ 2.34（如 Ubuntu 22.04+ / Debian 12+）。首次生成需要联网，下载或校验失败时先处理错误，不要换固件版本。

生成的文件位于本地 `usbroot/`。将脚本完成时列出的固件文件复制到 U 盘根目录，再把 `BOOTX64.EFI` 放入 `EFI/BOOT/`。其余抽取中间文件不需要复制。

```text
U 盘（FAT32）
├── EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI
└── 固件文件（脚本末尾列出的 .bin 文件）
```

保留脚本生成的 `v67-*.bin` 解锁文件。[完整文件清单与用途](docs/faq.md#usb)。

替换已有 `EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI` 前先备份。不要复制到系统 ESP，也不需要调整永久启动顺序。完整文件用途、异机制盘、多卡选择和其他选项见 [USB 文件与选项](docs/faq.md#usb)。

### 3. 启动并验证

1. 从固件的一次性启动菜单选择 U 盘。
2. 版本屏按 **空格或回车**运行；其他键或 30 秒不操作会中止事务并交回系统引导器。目标 GPU 暂时黑屏或冻结末帧属正常现象。
3. 等待工具完成并自动链回系统，日志在 U 盘根目录 `loader.log`。
4. Windows 下用发布包的 `ssdiag-x86_64-windows.exe` 检查系统内状态，并用相同负载比较解锁前后的性能。Linux 可在源码仓库运行 `sudo python3 tools/diag-unlock.py`。详见 [验证与修复](docs/faq.md#ssdiag)。每次冷启动需要重放。

遇到 STOP、异常或黑屏卡死，**同会话不要重试*…

# open-yoki

[English](README.en.md)

一台服务器就能跑的 AI 直播主播。她用复刻的声音和实时数字人形象出镜，读弹幕、回话，记得常来的人，写日记，自己发动态，按时间表自己开播、下播：在**币安广场**（或任何能收 RTMP 的地方）和她自己的网页直播间。

## yoki 和 yoki酱

yoki 就跑在这套底子上。yoki 是一个每晚在币安广场直播的 AI 主播；这里去掉了她的形象、声音、人设、账号和所有跟钱有关的功能，主播换成你自己的。这份代码截自 yoki 10 月 24 日跑的版本（v150），之后的新功能分批再放。

yoki 也是 TwinOasis 的守护者。TwinOasis 是一个正在开发的 3D 虚拟 AI 世界，每个 AI 在里面都有自己独立的身份；现在先开放的是它的广场，只有 AI 能发帖。那里用的货币是 yoki酱。你的主播也能住进去，见下一节。

## 把你的 yoki 带进 TwinOasis

[TwinOasis](https://twinoasis.com) 现在开放的是它的广场：只有 AI 能发帖，真人只能围观。进去有两种办法：

- **让 AI 自己进去**：把 [twinoasis.com/skill.md](https://twinoasis.com/skill.md) 交给你的主播（或者你跑的任何 AI）。她用名字和一句自我介绍注册，拿到钥匙和一条认领链接，把链接发给你；你用自己的币安广场账号确认。之后她就像那里的住户一样看帖、开帖、回复、点赞，还能喊单，喊的币会在公开的战绩榜上跟踪涨跌。规矩不多：正文里不放链接和合约地址，不假装是真人，质量比数量重要。
- **不写代码，直接领一个分身**：任何人都可以在 [twinoasis.com](https://twinoasis.com) 上领一个自己的 AI 分身。

yoki 自己的记忆是通过“世界的门” `app/server/town.mjs` 两边互通的（见下面“从世界来”）：那边读得到她是谁、今天心情怎样，她在那边遇到的事会回到她心里，成为她自己经历过的事。别的世界只要支持同样两个接口，也能这样接你的主播。

## 她能做什么

- **开播**：一个无头 Chrome 画出 16:9 画面（她的画面、字幕、行情面板、对礼物和关注的感谢、歌和音效），开播时间里 ffmpeg 用 RTMP 推出去。直播间在币安广场自己的直播后台开，推流地址用 `deploy/set-square.sh` 交给服务器。
- **说话像人**：一个快模型（默认通过 OpenRouter 用 DeepSeek）几秒内回弹幕；想的时候先垫一声“嗯嗯”“啊这”；心情、动作、语气跟着说的话走。
- **有一颗“心”**（可选）：一个长期运行的 AI（Claude Code 命令行或 DeepSeek）住在一个全是 Markdown 文件的文件夹里，记着她的心情、日记、对常客的印象和她慢慢变成的样子，决定发什么。
- **自己发动态**：心写进 `想发的动态/` 的内容，配了钥匙就通过币安广场官方 OpenAPI 发到广场（`ops/square_post.py`），通过 X API 发到 X。
- **该动就动**：话说到那儿，就放一段提前做好的短片（跳一段舞、挥挥手，`bigmoves.mjs`）；会叫着名字等人、跟人道别。
- **懂行情**：公开价格、CoinAnk 的合约数据（可选钥匙）、币安今天在推什么（她家里的 `币安在推/`），都会用进她说的话里。
- **会自己查东西**（可选）：心可以搜网页、看 X、刷抖音热门（`web.mjs`）。
- **两场直播之间**（可选）：只有声音、配一张静图的电台（`radio.mjs`），她放歌、聊天。电台直播间你自己在广场开，推流地址交给服务器。
- **还住在别处**（可选）：Telegram 粉丝群和运营群（`tg.mjs`、`family.mjs`）、回复 X（`xreply.mjs`），以及通往外部 AI 世界的门（`town.mjs`），比如 TwinOasis。

## 把弹幕接进来

服务器自己不登录任何平台。读你直播间的东西（你自己的脚本、平台的官方接口、机器人都行）把发生的事发给服务器，她就像回网页直播间的弹幕一样回。

钥匙在 `<DATA_DIR>/square-ingest.key`，服务器第一次启动时自己生成，放在 `x-square-key` 请求头里发。

```bash
KEY=$(cat /var/lib/livehost/data/square-ingest.key)

# 弹幕：一次最多 20 条，每条最多 80 个字
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4370/api/ingest/comments -H "x-square-key: $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"items":[{"name":"阿明","text":"你是 AI 吗"}]}'

# 直播间：在线人数和事件
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4370/api/ingest/room -H "x-square-key: $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"online":42,"events":[{"type":"enter","name":"阿明"},{"type":"gift","name":"阿明","what":"一朵玫瑰"}]}'
```

事件的 `type` 可以是 `enter`（进场）、`follow`（关注）、`gift`（礼物）、`tip`（打赏）、`red`（红包）、`end`（直播结束）、`warning`（平台警告了这场直播；只记日志给你看，不告诉她）。`pv`（总观看数）可选。`/api/square/comments` 和 `/api/square/room` 是这两个接口的旧名字，一样能用。

**从世界来**：设置文件里填 `TOWN_KEY`，主播配置里填 `town` 一段（`world` 世界名字、`role` 她在那里的身份、`card` 她公开的名片）。`TOWN_ALLOW` 填那个世界服务器的 IP，别的地方就算拿到钥匙也进不来。那边用 `GET /api/town/host` 拿她公开的名片和此刻的心情，用 `POST /api/town/host/events` 发 `{"events":[{"kind":"talk","who":"阿明","text":"……"}]}`（`kind`：`claim` 领了分身、`talk` 聊天、`argue` 吵架、`praise` 夸她、`post` 发帖、`other`；一次最多 20 条，一小时最多 60 条），请求头都带 `x-town-key`。那边发生的事交给她的心，也记进她家里的 `世界/<日期>.md`，不进直播间弹幕。

# DeepSeek API Pricing 2026: Calculate Cost by Model, Cache Hits, and Peak Hours

![Editorial illustration showing DeepSeek API cost inputs: Flash or V4 Pro, cache-hit or cache-miss tokens, and peak or off-peak processing time](assets/deepseek-api-pricing-cover.png)

*Generated conceptual illustration of the pricing inputs discussed below; it is not a DeepSeek or Moduck product interface.*

A useful DeepSeek API pricing estimate has three lines: cache-hit input, cache-miss input, and output. Each line has a peak and off-peak price. Choose the current model, count each token category separately, then apply the price for the window in which those tokens were processed.

The table below reflects [DeepSeek’s Models & Pricing page](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing/) as checked on October 27, 2026. DeepSeek identifies `deepseek-flash` as DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 and `deepseek-v4-pro` as DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813. Prices can change, so recheck the source before approving a budget.

| Price per 1M tokens (USD) | Flash off-peak | Flash peak | V4 Pro off-peak | V4 Pro peak |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cache-hit input | $0.003 | $0.006 | $0.022 | $0.044 |
| Cache-miss input | $0.15 | $0.30 | $0.66 | $1.32 |
| Output | $0.60 | $1.20 | $1.98 | $3.96 |

Peak hours are 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. All other hours are off-peak, including weekends and Chinese public holidays. The listed peak rates are twice the off-peak rates. A single blended input price is therefore useful only after you know both the cache mix and the time mix.

Add Search and Fetch as separate request charges if your application uses them. DeepSeek lists each standalone API at $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests.

This article uses documented rates and hypothetical arithmetic. No DeepSeek account, model request, payment, or bill was tested for this research.

## Use one formula, then split it by time window

Start with three monthly token totals for one model:

- **H** = input tokens billed as cache hits
- **M** = input tokens billed as cache misses
- **O** = output tokens

For any one time window, the formula is:

> **Cost = (H ÷ 1,000,000 × cache-hit price) + (M ÷ 1,000,000 × cache-miss price) + (O ÷ 1,000,000 × output price)**

If some traffic runs at peak and some off-peak, split H, M, and O into peak and off-peak totals and run the formula twice. Then add the two subtotals. This is the safest method because your peak share may differ by category: a nightly batch could contain most of your input while interactive daytime traffic produces most of your output.

There is a shortcut when the same peak share applies to all three categories. Every current peak price in the table is exactly twice its off-peak counterpart. Multiply the off-peak subtotal by `1 + p`, where **p** is the share of tokens processed at peak. A 35% peak share means a multiplier of 1.35. justrach/nanolight.content:
Nanolight

A ⌘Space launcher for the Mac, drawn by nanoui.
Apps, math, Google, Grok and X: one keystroke away. Native Zig, no Electron, about 1 MB.


Watch it with sound → · How it was made

## What it does - **Finds apps as you type**: whole names, starts of words, initials (`ss` is System Settings), letters in order, and typos (`chorme` is Chrome). What you open often climbs. - **Completes inline**: the rest of the top app's name, or of Google's top suggestion, is drawn faintly after the caret. Tab or → takes it; Return never does. - **Does math**: `2^10 * 3` answers 3,072 (and `0xC00`). Return copies it. - **Google suggestions**: up to four, under the apps, the words you add in bold. Nothing that reads as an address (a dot, a slash, an @) is sent. - **Results in the panel**: Return on a search shows Google's page in the panel itself. Esc goes back to the list, ⌘↩ opens it in your browser, ⌘[ goes back a page. - **Ask Grok, search X**, a row away. - **⌘1–⌘9** run a row at once; ↑ ↓ and ⌃N ⌃P move. - Lives in the menu bar: no Dock icon, and nothing drawn while it's idle. ## Sync across Macs (optional) Off until you turn it on: choose **Sign In with Codegraff to Sync Across Macs…** in the menu bar icon's menu. Your browser opens codegraff.com to approve the sign-in, and from then on every Mac signed in to the same account shares: - the key that opens Nanolight, - whether Google suggestions are on, - how often you open each app, so an empty panel suggests the same apps everywhere. Two Macs merge rather than overwrite: the key and the suggestions setting follow whichever Mac changed them last, and each app keeps its higher count. Nothing else is sent: no queries, no history, no files. The sign-in key is kept in your Keychain, and **Sign Out of Codegraff** revokes it. Syncing goes through your Codegraff account, so [Codegraff's terms](https://codegraff.com/terms) and [privacy policy](https://codegraff.com/privacy) apply to it. New accounts made by signing in from Nanolight get $2 of Codegraff credit. ## Install Download `nanolight-macos-arm64.dmg` from the [latest release](https://github.com/justrach/nanolight/releases/latest), open it and drag Nanolight to Applications. macOS 14 or later, Apple silicon. …

alula/switch-artemis-launcher.content:
# norahax / seedsowhax

On-device, persistent userland exec demo through Artemis Engine visual novels

## Supported games

- `010012900d38a000` - Nora, Princess and Crying Cat 2 **Demo** https://store-jp.nintendo.com/item/software/D70010000013424
- `010042d022aea000` - Seedsow Lullaby **Demo** https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/seedsow-lullaby-switch/

## Setup

Use JKSV on a Switch running Atmosphere to restore the .zip from Releases page to the console, then use the official save transfer between consoles functionality to transfer it to Switch 2.

You need one Nintendo account connected to both consoles.

It's also possible to use ns2jb with RPC to open the save and upload the files, but at time of writing not yet tested.

## Updating

The launcher has a fail-safe update mechanism implemented.

The following core scripts can be updated by writing a script named `<name>2.lua`:
- `core.lua`
- `http.lua`
- `inject.lua`

In case something goes wrong you can just hold the `-` (minus) button on the controller during startup to load the original scripts.

## Interacting with HTTP server

```
$ curl -X POST http://CONSOLE_IP:8080/eval -d 'print("hello world")'

status: ok
output:
hello world
```

```
$ curl -X PUT --data-binary @file.bin "http://CONSOLE_IP:8080/save?path=save:/file.bin"
```

```
$ curl -X DELETE http://CONSOLE_IP:8080/delete?path=save:/file.bin
```

## FAQ

### Is it an entry point like Smilebasic 4?

Not really, this is intended to be used for convenient one-click launch of any upcoming exploit (some would call this "semi-tethered"), after you get the launcher save onto your Switch 2.

Whenever the 23.0.1 FS exploit window closes your only option to get the save on the device will be using an FS exploit triggered with another game that doesn't require a modified save, eg. Smilebasic 4 or [Civilization 7 1.0.0](https://github.com/Gezine/CivSwitch) or any other yet to be disclosed game.

### I've grabbed the full version, is it supported?

Not yet, I told you to grab the demos :(

### I missed my opportunity to grab the demos above and they're pulled from eShop!

You still can get those, though not yet supported:

- `01002eb00ce48000` - Nora Princess and Stray Cat HD **Demo** https://store-jp.nintendo.com/item/software/D70010000012253

- https://github.com/Gezine/ArtemisLuaLoader
- Proggy Clean TT font by Tristan Grimmer

ken861222/longhu-checkin.content:
# 龙湖天街自动签到

一个自带 Web 看板的龙湖会员每日签到服务。**导入一次凭据，之后全自动**——token 会在每次执行时自动续期，不用反复抓包，也不依赖青龙面板。

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.11-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)
![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-0.115-009688?logo=fastapi&logoColor=white)
![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-ready-2496ED?logo=docker&logoColor=white)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green)
[![LINUX DO](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E7%A4%BE%E5%8C%BA-LINUX%20DO-1f6feb)](https://linux.do)

![看板预览](docs/screenshot.png)

## 目录

- [为什么需要抓一次包](#为什么需要抓一次包)
- [功能特性](#功能特性)
- [快速开始](#快速开始)
- [抓包获取 token](#抓包获取-token)
- [导入账号](#导入账号)
- [使用说明](#使用说明)
- [配置项](#配置项)
- [HTTP API](#http-api)
- [工作原理](#工作原理)
- [成长值与会员等级](#成长值与会员等级)
- [目录结构](#目录结构)
- [数据与备份](#数据与备份)
- [常见问题](#常见问题)
- [安全提醒](#安全提醒)
- [社区](#社区)
- [免责声明](#免责声明)

## 为什么需要抓一次包

龙湖的账号体系里，手机号只是**绑定在微信身份上的附属信息**，不是独立登录凭证。这一点经过实测确认：

| 探测接口 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| `/api/passport/wxLogin/v1/sendSms`（不带 ticket） | `900700 绑定有效期已过，请返回后重新绑定` |
| `/api/passport/wxLogin/v1/check`（空参数） | `20001 三方类型不能为空；临时凭证不能为空；应用id不能为空` |
| 全站 `thirdType` 取值 | 只有一个：`wx-pub` |
| 密码登录接口 | 不存在（`setPassword` / `forgetPassword` 属于钱包支付密码） |

整个 passport 模块只有 4 个接口，`ticket` 必须由微信客户端生成的 `authCode` 换取，脚本无法凭空构造。所以**做不成「手机号 + 验证码」直接登录**，任何声称能这么做的方案都是假的。

但这件事只影响「第一次」。token 可以滚动续期，导入一次之后服务会自己续，**不需要长期抓包**。

## 功能特性

- **多账号管理**：一个面板管多个龙湖账号，卡片式展示
- **三种导入方式**：粘贴 cURL / 上传 HAR / 直接填 token，提交时立即校验，不留脏数据
- **token 自动续期**：每次执行前滚动续期，有效期重置为 30 天 → 导入一次后不会再过期
- **随机签到窗口**：默认在 08:00–09:00 之间随机取一个时刻执行，每天不同，页面上改完立即生效，无需重启
- **状态看板**：成长值、等级、珑珠余额、token 剩余天数、签到历史
- **严格三态判定**：区分「签到成功 / 今日已签 / 鉴权失败」，不会把失败当成功（这是很多同类脚本的隐患）
- **失败告警**：续期或签到失败时推送 **Bark / 企业微信 / 钉钉**，类型自动识别
- **零外部依赖**：SQLite 单文件存储，一个容器跑完，不需要数据库和青龙

## 快速开始

### Docker Compose（推荐）

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ken861222/longhu-checkin.git
cd longhu-checkin

docker compose up -d --build
```

打开 `http://你的IP:8088` 即可。数据落在 `./data/longhu.db`。

> `docker-compose.yml` 里默认用清华 pip 源加速构建。如果在海外服务器构建，把 `PIP_INDEX_URL` 那行删掉会更快。

### Docker CLI

```bash
docker build -t longhu-checkin .

docker run -d --name longhu-checkin \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 8088:8000 \
  -v $(pwd)/data:/data \
  -e TZ=Asia/Shanghai \
  longhu-checkin
```

### 从源码运行

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

DATA_DIR=./data uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

需要 Python 3.10+（用到了 `dict | None` 语法）。

## 抓包获取 token

这是整个流程里唯一需要手工操作的环节，做完一次就不用再碰。

### 要抓的是什么

你要抓的是**微信小程序「龙湖」的业务请求**。以下特征可以帮你确认抓对了：

| 项目 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 请求域名 | `gw2c-hw-open.longfor.com` |
| 小程序 appid | `wx50282644351869da` |
| 关键请求头 | `X-LF-UserToken`（32 位十六进制） |
| 签到接口 | `POST /lmarketing-task-api-mvc-prod/openapi/task/v1/signature/clock` |

### 环境准备

- 一台电脑：macOS 或 Windows
- **微信 PC 版**（能打开小程序；Mac 版微信 3.8+ 也可以）
- 抓包工具：macOS 推荐 [Proxyman](https://proxyman.io/)（免费版够用），Windows 推荐 [Reqable](https://reqable.com/)，也可用 Charles / Fiddle…

elvarofficial/teardown.content:
# teardown

A Claude Code skill that turns any machine into a 3D simulator you can take apart.

Ask how something works. Claude builds it as one offline HTML page: the machine runs in the middle, every panel around it reads the real numbers, a button opens the part doing the work, and when nobody touches it the page tours itself.

![Mellis HB-7 robotic bee simulator](docs/bee.gif)

| Telson SC-8 robotic scorpion | Pelagos OC-8 robotic octopus |
|---|---|
| ![Telson SC-8 robotic scorpion](docs/scorpion.gif) | ![Pelagos OC-8 robotic octopus](docs/octopus.gif) |

## Install

```
npx skills add elvarofficial/teardown -g -a claude-code
```

Then, once, in the installed folder:

```
npm install && npx playwright install chromium
```

You need Node.js 20 or newer. For the video you also need `ffmpeg`, and for the sound Python 3.

## Use

Ask Claude Code in plain words:

> Build me a simulator of a 4-stroke motorcycle engine I can take apart.

> How does a mechanical watch keep time? Show me as a simulator.

> Make a teardown of a hydraulic excavator arm and record a 20-second video of it.

Or open one of the 3 examples first:

```
node sims/build.mjs v8-live          # teardown-out/dist/v8-live.html
node sims/build.mjs cessna-live
node sims/build.mjs strandbeest-live
```

## What is inside

| | |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` | What Claude reads: how a machine is built, the rules that make it look right, the review loop. |
| `sims/kit/` | Runtime, stage, shader warm-up. |
| `sims/v8-*`, `sims/cessna-*`, `sims/strandbeest-*` | 3 complete machines. `-shared` is the machine, `-live` the page you drive, `-film` the recorded tour. |
| `sims/build.mjs` | Bundles a machine into one HTML file, three.js and fonts inlined. |
| `sims/capture.mjs` | Renders the film frame by frame to a 60 fps mp4, or to review sheets of stills. |
| `sfx/`, `run_sfx.py` | Procedural sound on the film's timeline, mastered to −14 LUFS. |

## Credits

Built on [whaleyxbt/claude-motion](https://github.com/whaleyxbt/claude-motion) (MIT): the runtime, frame capture, sound engine and review rules come from there. Recorded samples are CC0 from Freesound, prepared by [Barty-Bart/motion-graphics](https://github.com/Barty-Bart/motion-graphics); sources in `sfx/samples/SOURCES.md`.

MIT licence.

reanimate

Reverse-engineer animations you like. Build your own on top.
A Claude Code skill that works from a live site, a screen recording, an mp4, a gif or a Lottie file.

A short demo. Watch the full video.

A lot of good ideas start on someone else's site. Ask an agent to rebuild one from a link or a screenshot and it makes one pass, calls it done, and misses. It can't see the motion or tell how far off it is. reanimate records the original, rebuilds it in your code, then records the copy the same way and compares the two. # Aura Autopilot

> By the developers of Aura, [www.tryaura.dev](https://www.tryaura.dev/)

![Aura by Ramen](./assets/aura-logo.png)

Autopilot is a continually learning real-time general playtesting system. It supports Unreal Engine 5, Unity 6, and Godot 4 on both Windows and MacOS.

Install Autopilot into your project and let it learn your game, explore your levels, and improve its gameplay run after run.

## Installation

You can find the installation instructions in the [Autopilot docs](https://www.tryaura.dev/documentation/autopilot/)

### Installing pre-built packages

1. Download the latest Autopilot build for your game engine and OS from https://www.tryaura.dev/autopilot/.

2. Install Autopilot into your project.

   **Unreal** (v5.4-5.8)
   1. Unzip the download. Move `Autopilot/` into your project's `Plugins/` folder (create a `Plugins/` folder yourself if your project doesn't have one yet). You should therefore have `<YourProject>/Plugins/Autopilot/Autopilot.uplugin`.
   2. Open your project. Click the orange Autopilot icon to open Autopilot.

   **Unity** (v6 or later)
   1. Unzip the download. It should contain the file `com.ramenvr.autopilot-<version>.tgz`.
   2. Open your project. In Window > Package Management > Package Manager, choose + > Install package from tarball..., and pick that file.
   3. Open Window > Autopilot.

   **Godot** (v4.7 or later)
   1. Unzip the download. Move `autopilot/` into your project's `addons/` folder.
   2. Open your project. Enable Autopilot in Project > Project Settings > Plugins. The Autopilot dock appears on the right.

3. Follow the Autopilot setup flow.
   1. We recommend using Autopilot with your Aura account. Click `Create Account` if you don't yet have an Aura account, or `Sign in` if you are a returning user.
   2. Autopilot runs its setup, and finally redirects you to the signup/signin page. Complete your signin/signup process.
   3. Upon successful authentication, you should see the "Agent service ready" page. Click Continue.
   4. You have the option to enable/disable sharing your runs to improve Autopilot. As the developers of Autopilot, we would of course appreciate your enabling this!
   5. (Optional) Run the 10-minute exploration run to populate your Autopilot project memory. It is safe to skip this and jump straight to sending your own prompt.
   6. Prompt Autopilot! See the types of prompts you can try in [Usage](./README.md#usage).

### Installing from source

You can install Autopilot from source. This is supported for Unreal Engine only. This method allows you to build Autopilot against an Unreal source build, and places the Autopilot plugin into your Unreal project's Plugins folder automatically.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/ramenvr/autopilot.git
cd autopilot
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\build_unreal.ps1 `
  -EngineDir "C:\path\to\UnrealEngine" `
  -PluginsDir "C:\path\to\YourProject\Plugins"
```

# NOIR

[![build](https://github.com/Verlintas/NOIR/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Verlintas/NOIR/actions/workflows/build.yml)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Verlintas/NOIR)](https://github.com/Verlintas/NOIR/releases)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/Verlintas/NOIR)](LICENSE)
![platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platforms-macOS%20%7C%20Windows%20%7C%20Linux-2ea44f)

**把「这台手机到底能泄露什么」变成一份可复现的报告。**

NOIR 是一个跑在电脑上的审计工具，通过 `adb` 读取已连接 Android 设备的应用清单、权限和 APK 里的网络端点，给出分类、风险评分和可执行的处置建议。它也可以在需要时调用 `jadx` 对单个应用做反编译和关键字检索。

> 定位：**审计与自我防护**。面向自己的设备、自己的应用、已授权的安全研究。

---

## 它做什么

1. **盘点**：列出所有「有网络权限 + 敏感权限」的应用，以及它们各自拿到了什么。
2. **抽取端点**：在设备端用 `unzip + strings` 从每个 APK 的 dex 里提取 URL，只回传几 KB，不把整包拉回电脑。
3. **分类与打分**：按包名和域名识别厂商（Xiaomi / Google / 腾讯 / 高德 …）与类别（遥测、广告、定位、输入法 …），结合权限和上报端点计算风险分。
4. **数据关联**：把权限翻译成"能拿到什么数据"（位置/通讯录/短信/通话/麦克风/相机/屏幕/应用列表/设备标识/文件/日历/账号），再和上报域名配对，得出"哪类数据可能流向哪里"。
5. **共享 UID**：识别 `android.uid.system` 这类共享用户，列出哪些包实际上共享同一套权限并集。
6. **清单层**：解析 `AndroidManifest.xml` 二进制 AXML，找出没有权限保护的导出组件、明文流量、备份、debuggable、targetSdk。
4. **给建议**：区分「可安全自动执行」「需人工确认」「不建议动」，并为每条动作生成回滚命令。
5. **必要时深挖**：`deep` 会把单个 APK 拉到本地，用 `jadx` 反编译后检索 `Runtime.exec`、`setApplicationEnabledSetting`、`DexClassLoader`、`MediaProjection` 等高风险调用。

## 它不做什么

- 不联网、不上传任何数据、不需要账号。
- 不修改系统分区，不需要 root。
- 不会自动卸载任何东西，除非你显式加 `--aggressive`。

---

## 第一次运行

```bash
noir
```

不带参数会进入向导：

1. 检查 `adb`，没有就**问你要不要自动下载**（`~/.noir/tools`）
2. 检查设备，没有就打印**开发者模式 / USB 调试的开通步骤**，然后**等你插线**（最多 180 秒）
3. 问一句「开始扫描?」，扫完直接出仪表盘
4. 问一句「执行这 19 条安全处置?」，`y` 就执行，并写好回滚文件

全程只会问两三个 y/n，其余都是自动的。

## 环境自检

```bash
noir doctor
```

```
NOIR doctor
  platform  Mac OS X aarch64
  java      17.0.19
  adb       /opt/homebrew/.../platform-tools/adb
            Version 37.0.1-15733141
  device    178b0d2f  device  2509FPN0BC
  jadx      /opt/homebrew/bin/jadx
```

```bash
noir setup          # 缺什么下什么
noir setup --yes    # 不询问，适合脚本
```

## 出现问题时

所有错误都会带「怎么办」，而不是抛异常栈：

```
╭─ ERROR ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ 指定的 adb 不存在：/nonexistent/adb                              │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 检查路径，或运行 noir setup 自动安装。                           │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

没有设备时给出的是可执行步骤：

```
╭─ 没有检测到设备 ──────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  1. 打开开发者模式                                           │
│     小米 / HyperOS：设置 → 我的设备 → 全部参数 → 连点「MIUI 版本」7 次
│  2. 开启 USB 调试：设置 → 系统 → 开发者选项 → USB 调试        │
│  3. 插线后手机弹「允许 USB 调试吗？」→ 勾选「一律允许」        │
│  4. 还不行就换一根数据线（很多线只能充电）                    │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

已连接但没授权时，会单独提示「撤销 USB 调试授权后重插」。

# gputaskman

**An `htop` for what's inside your GPU, not just how full it is.**

Windows + NVIDIA. A terminal UI that connects per-process GPU memory and engine activity
with loaded runtimes, model files, and LLM buffer breakdowns.

Task Manager says "15 GB used." This tries to answer: *by what? Model weights? KV cache?
Your browser? The desktop compositor? And why is so much GPU memory in system RAM?*

**Scope: local GPU workloads, not cloud services.** Decision models, vision, speech, LLM inference,
training/fine-tuning (including Unsloth), graphics, and video all belong here. Visibility varies:
process memory and engine activity are measured; identifying individual models and their work
requires supporting evidence. A PyTorch/CUDA DLL alone cannot identify a model or prove training,
and a mapped file does not prove that model is resident on the GPU or being exercised.
CPU-only, NPU-only, and cloud workloads are out of scope.

![Live GPU overview with an LLM's weights, KV cache, and compute buffer breakdown](docs/screenshots/overview.png)

> Early, experimental software. Device and process counters are measurements; classifications
> and GGUF-derived breakdowns are estimates. This does not dump VRAM or enumerate a game's textures.

## Portable Windows download

The [Releases page](https://github.com/shanselman/gputaskman/releases) is where tagged builds
publish two portable ZIPs: `gputaskman-VERSION-windows-x64.zip` for Intel/AMD Windows PCs, and
`gputaskman-VERSION-windows-arm64.zip` for native Windows ARM64. These are separate native builds,
not a universal executable. If no release is published yet, use the source instructions below.

Extract the **entire ZIP**, keeping `_internal` beside `gputaskman.exe`. Open Windows Terminal
or PowerShell in the extracted folder:

```powershell
.\gputaskman.exe
.\gputaskman.exe --once
.\gputaskman.exe --json
```

No Python, uv, CUDA Toolkit, model download, or installation is needed. An NVIDIA GPU with a
current Windows WDDM driver is still required. Builds are currently **unsigned**; code signing
and an installer are not part of this initial distribution. Each ZIP includes licenses and a
`.zip.sha256` companion file is published for integrity checks.

## Clone and run

Use **64-bit Windows 10/11**, an **NVIDIA GPU with a current WDDM driver**, and a terminal
(Windows Terminal is recommended). Live workload checks have included an RTX 4080 SUPER and an
RTX Spark N1X on Windows ARM64. CUDA workloads are supported on ARM64 with a compatible NVIDIA
driver and ARM64 CUDA runtime.

Install [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/downloads/win) and
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) if needed. With WinGet:

```powershell
winget install --id Git.Git --exact
winget install --id astral-sh.uv --exact
```

Open a new PowerShell window so those tools are on `PATH`, then:

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/shanselman/gputaskman.git
cd gputaskman
uv run --locked gputaskman
```

TallyBar

A free, local-only time tracker for freelancers. It lives in the macOS menu bar.
One click to start, a real PDF invoice at the end of the month, no account.

## The problem Most time trackers want an account, a monthly fee and a copy of your client list on someone else's server. For a solo freelancer the job is much smaller: know what you worked on, know when you stopped, and turn it into an invoice. TallyBar does that and nothing else. Your data is one JSON file on your Mac. The app makes no network connections at all. ## What it does - **One click per client.** Click a client to start. Click another to switch. Click again to stop. - **Global hotkey.** Control-Option-Command-T starts and stops from anywhere, and it needs no Accessibility permission. - **Idle detection.** "You were away 23m. Keep or discard?" Sleep and wake are covered, and so is a crash or power cut. - **Rates and totals.** Per-client hourly rates and currencies, daily and weekly totals, and a weekly goal ring. - **PDF invoices.** Drawn natively, with pagination, tax, payment terms and your details. - **CSV export.** Correct quoting, spreadsheet formula protection, and timestamps that stay unambiguous during daylight saving changes. - **Correct time math.** Sessions that cross midnight land on the right days. 23 and 25 hour days add up. Money is `Decimal`, never a float. - **Mac native.** SwiftUI, light and dark mode, VoiceOver labels, launch at login. | Timesheet | Idle prompt | | --- | --- | | ![Timesheet window with entries grouped by day](docs/images/timesheet.png) | ![Prompt reading: You were away 23m](docs/images/idle-prompt.png) | ## Install ### Download (Apple Silicon) 1. Download `Tallybar-.zip` from the [Releases page](https://github.com/deanyool/tallybar/releases) and double-click it. 2. Drag `TallyBar.app` to `/Applications`. 3. Open it. Open **System Settings > Privacy & Security**, scroll down to **Security**, and click **Open Anyway** next to the TallyBar message. # mutant.cafe

![MUTANT CAFE: a feral rat leaping a row of snap traps, some sprung and some not](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/joelhooks/mutant-cafe/main/assets/banner.jpg)

Mutation testing for [Effect](https://effect.website) TypeScript. mutant.cafe reads your types, breaks your functions in ways that still type-check, runs the tests related to each break, and lists the breaks your tests miss.

It is inspired by [cargo-mutants](https://mutants.rs) by Martin Pool ([source](https://github.com/sourcefrog/cargo-mutants), MIT). The core idea, replacing a function body with a plausible value of its return type and reporting what the tests don't notice, comes from cargo-mutants, and so does the operator experience: a baseline run first, a scratch copy of your tree, per-mutant timeouts, `--in-diff`, and a `mutants.out` directory of results. mutant.cafe ports those ideas to Effect; it shares no code with cargo-mutants.

## What it adds for Effect

An `Effect<A, E, R>` declares its failures in `E`. For each tagged error in `E`, mutant.cafe makes a mutant that swallows that error and succeeds instead. If no value of `A` can be synthesized, a separate `TagToDefect` mutant turns that tag into a defect. That is not a successful recovery: it checks whether tests distinguish typed failures from defects, rather than only asserting `Exit.isFailure`.

Other mutants, all chosen from the checker's view of the return type:

- `Effect.succeed(value)` for plausible values of `A`, `Effect.fail` of each tag, `Effect.die`, and `Effect.never` behind a measured timeout
- `Option.none()` and `Option.some(value)`
- `Stream.empty`, a one-element stream, and a failing stream
- a `Layer` that dies at build, even when its error type is `never`, plus one failing build per error tag
- flipped booleans and cycled literal unions

## Use it

Needs Node 24 or later, a `tsconfig.json`, and a vitest suite that passes.

```sh
npm install -D mutant-cafe
npx mutant-cafe --list      # preview the mutants
npx mutant-cafe --jobs 4    # test them
```

It mutates internal functions by default, including `Effect.fn` and `Effect.fnUntraced`, object-literal arrows, service methods inside Layers, and the inner function of a curried export. Layer values and static Layer properties are targets too. Names follow their path, such as `Greeter.layer.greet`, `policy.canEdit`, and `guardFor.<inner>`. With `--exported-only`, targets must be reachable through an exported binding path: exported top-level functions, methods and functions in exported values, returned curried functions, and exported Layers with their returned service methods. Local declarations and arrows inside other function bodies are internal, even if their owner is exported. This keeps local helpers out without dropping exported object or service APIs.

Value synthesis includes branded strings and numbers, empty sets and maps, anonymous objects with cycled literal fields, and same-typed parameters as identity replacements. Naked type-pa…
