# Abyssal Garden

**A dreamy underwater world you can swim through, right in your browser.**

Towering kelp forests, sunbeams pouring through a rippling surface, a sunken ship, manta rays gliding overhead.
And all of it is made by code: no images, no 3D models, no sound files. The whole world fits in **one 96 KB HTML file**.

![Kelp forest with a stone whale tail and a manta ray](.github/screenshots/whale-fluke.jpg)

## Try it

1. Download [`index.html`](index.html).
2. Open it in **Chrome** or **Edge** on a desktop computer.
3. Wait a few seconds while the world is built, then press **Dive in** and start swimming.

Nothing to install, and it works offline. It needs a browser with **WebGPU**. If you see *"This scene needs WebGPU"*, update your browser or switch to Chrome / Edge.

## What's down there

- **Kelp forests** that sway in the current and sparkle with tiny gold and green specks
- **Light rays** streaming down from a wavy surface, with shimmering caustics on the sea floor
- **A sunken wooden ship**, a **giant stone whale tail**, rock arches, canyons and floating boulders
- **Manta rays**, schools of fish, rising bubbles and drifting particles
- **A purple grotto** with glowing magenta ground cover, coral and barrel sponges
- **A soundscape** made up as you listen: a deep rumble, distant whale calls, soft chimes and bubbles

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Shipwreck](.github/screenshots/shipwreck.jpg) | ![Looking up through the kelp](.github/screenshots/kelp-forest.jpg) |

| Up / down | `E` / `Q` |
| Swim faster | Hold `Shift` |
| Jump to a viewpoint | `1` to `6` (the spots in the screenshots) |
| Menu | `Esc` releases the mouse and opens the menu with the list of controls; **Resume** takes you back |
| Sound on / off | `M` (sound starts when you dive in) |
| Performance stats | `H` |
| Detail level | **Low**, **Medium** or **High** in the menu (reloads the page) |

The seabed, cliffs and arches are solid: you glide along the rock instead of swimming into it, and you still fit through every tunnel and arch. Kelp, plants, corals, sponges, loose rocks, the floating boulders, the ship and the whale tail you can swim through.

**On a touchscreen:** hold one finger down to swim forward and slide it to steer. Put a second finger down to go faster. The `≡` button in the corner opens the menu. Phones always show the scene in landscape and start on Low or Medium detail. (Touch support is experimental.)

# gpucanvas

Put thousands of live DOM nodes on an infinite canvas: the GPU draws them, an editor selects,
moves and resizes them, shaders and transitions run on them, and an AI agent can read them and
point at them.

![The same 5,000 live React screens as plain DOM (left) and in gpucanvas (right), with each side's frame rate measured live](docs/benchmark.gif)

The same session on both sides: 5,000 live React screens, the same camera path, a message typed and sent. Left, every screen is plain DOM under a CSS transform. Right, gpucanvas. Recorded in Chrome on a MacBook Pro; the frame rates are measured live in each run. Run it yourself in the [live demo](https://berkantay.github.io/gpucanvas/).

- **[Canvas](#how-it-works).** Live React or plain DOM nodes, drawn by WebGPU in one instanced
  pass. Pan and zoom never touch the DOM, and clicks, typing and state still reach the real
  elements.
- **[Editor](#editing).** Click to select, double-click to go a layer deeper, down to any element
  or React component. Move and resize with snapping guides.

# PeakCut

Turn long videos and live streams into captioned vertical clips, ready to post. Free and open source: run it on
your own computer or server, with your own AI key.

Paste a YouTube, Twitch or Kick link (or upload a file) and PeakCut finds the moments worth clipping, cuts them to
9:16, adds word-by-word captions and a hook, and can post them to your connected accounts. It can also record a
creator's live stream and clip the highlights while the stream is still running.

## What it does

- **Clips from any video.** Transcribes the audio, asks an AI which moments would hold a stranger's attention, and
  renders each one with captions in one of three styles.
- **Live clipping.** Records a stream into a rolling buffer and clips as it happens, using loudness, chat activity
  and the transcript.
- **Workspaces per creator.** Channels, clip settings, posting rules and an activity log for each creator you clip.
- **Posting.** Connect YouTube, Instagram and TikTok in one click, then queue or auto-post finished clips, with
  spacing and daily caps (see [DEPLOY.md](DEPLOY.md#connecting-youtube-instagram-and-tiktok) for the one-time setup).
- **No sign-in on your own computer.** It opens straight into the dashboard. On a shared server, switch accounts on
  (`PEAKCUT_ACCOUNTS=1`) for email or Google sign-in and an admin dashboard.
- **Your own AI.** Gemini, OpenAI, Grok, Groq, OpenRouter, Claude, a local model through Ollama, or anything that
  speaks the OpenAI chat format. No key at all also works: clips are then picked by loudness.

## Quick start

You need Python 3.10 or newer and `ffmpeg`. On Windows: `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`. On a Mac: `brew install ffmpeg`.
On Linux: `sudo apt install ffmpeg`. PeakCut finds it by itself and tells you in the dashboard if it is missing.

```bash
git clone <this repository> peakcut
```

```bash
cd peakcut
```

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Start the server:

```bash
python -m studio.server
```

The first start downloads the speech model by itself (about 480 MB, once).

Open http://127.0.0.1:8765. There is no sign-in: it opens straight into the dashboard. Go to **Settings, AI**, choose
your AI service, paste your key and press **Save and test** (see [Choose your AI](#choose-your-ai)).

## Choose your AI

PeakCut needs a chat model that can return JSON. The easy way is in the dashboard: **Settings, AI**. Pick the
service, paste your key, press **Find models** to choose from the service's own list, then **Save and test**. The
key is kept in the data folder on your machine and is never shown again.

If you prefer a file (or run a server), the same three things can go in `.env`. What is saved in the dashboard wins:

```ini
PEAKCUT_AI_PROVIDER=gemini
PEAKCUT_AI_MODELS=gemini-2.5-flash
PEAKCUT_AI_KEY=your-key-here
```

# Muse JP Reg (muse.ai 批量自动注册与邀请码裂变系统)

基于 [`duwqijlk/muse-protocol`](https://github.com/duwqijlk/muse-protocol) 纯 HTTP 协议链路实现，集成独立管理控制台（WebUI）、粘性代理调度、多接码源与邀请码裂变池，专用于 **`muse.ai`** 的批量注册、会话激活、邀请码兑换与自有码自动回收。

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **节点地区建议**：请优先使用 **日本 (JP) 代理节点**（免绑卡直接通过引导）；非开放地区引导后会进入 `waitlist` 候补状态。

---

## 一、核心功能

1. **纯 HTTP 浏览器对齐协议栈 (`musepy/` + `auth_flow.py`)**
   - `GET /`：按真实 Chrome 跨站重定向规则跟随 `aymh` 跳转链路，获取 `datr` / `ig_did` 等基础 Cookie，并校验客户端态标识。
   - `POST /api/auth/native/restart`：生成全程共用的 `X-Hatch-Waterfall-Id` 并获取 `csrf_token`。
   - `POST /api/auth/native/send-otp` + 幂等 OTP 轮询（`mail_providers/`）：支持本地 `4173` iCloud 中转工作台、`[{"otp","time"}]` 标准化 JSON 源、第三方中转链接、Cloudflare Temp Mail 及 Outlook IMAP/Graph。
   - `POST /api/auth/native/confirm-otp`：自动提取服务端动态 `tos.content_version`。
   - `POST /api/auth/native/register-completion`：自动生成成年日本用户档案，成功后**立即早落盘**核心凭证（`frl_account_id`、`frl_access_token`、`hatch_sess`）。
   - `POST auth.meta.com/hatch/session/bootstrap/`：手动跟随受信 3xx 跳转，离线解析 Next Flight 动态披露（`disclosureText` / `disclosureVersion`）与地区状态门。
   - `POST /api/hatch/accept-tos` + `vm/wake` + `stateful-sharing`：激活 Hatch 会话并唤醒云端 VM。
   - `POST /api/hatch/invite-code/redeem` + `POST /api/hatch/invite`：兑换池内邀请码并取回本账号专属 `own_code`，支持**自动入池裂变（1 裂变 30）**。

2. **Sticky 代理调度与停批保护 (`webui/auto_loop.py`)**
   - Worker 独占认领代理节点，兼容 `host:port:user:pass`、`http://`、`socks5://`（自动转远端 DNS `socks5h://`）。
   - 支持 `max_per_ip` 成号计数轮换；发码前传输层失败自动黑名单并同邮箱换代理重试（最多 3 次）。
   - 遇 `region_waitlist`、服务端拒绝或邀请码耗尽自动暂停并推送告警横幅，防止烧号。

3. **Vue 3 + Element Plus 管理后台 (`webui/`)**
   - 仪表盘、邮箱导入与同步、邀请码池管理、单次注册实时日志流、全自动批量调度、已注册账号存货检测与补兑/导出、代理池测试与管理。

---

## 二、快速开始

### 1. 安装依赖

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

如需重新构建前端静态资源：

```bash
cd webui/frontend
npm install
npm run build
```

### 2. 启动控制台

```bash
python start_webui.py --port 8766
```

启动后访问：`http://127.0.0.1:8766`

（Windows 环境也可直接使用根目录下的 `启动服务.bat` / `停止服务.bat`。）

### 3. 本地 iCloud 邮箱同步（可选）

如果同级目录运行了本地 iCloud 隐藏邮箱服务（默认 `../icloud/data/workbench.db`，可通过环境变量 `ICLOUD_DB_PATH` 覆盖）：

```bash
python import_icloud.py --limit 10
```

脚本仅领取尚未分配取件密钥的新邮箱（`token_hash IS NULL`），不会覆盖其他系统已使用的密钥。

---

## 三、离线冒烟测试

```bash
python test_onboarding_smoke.py
python test_runner_smoke.py
python test_webui_smoke.py
```

---

## 四、免责声明

本项目仅供个人学习与协议研究使用，请严格遵守目标站点的服务条款及相关法律法规。

# 用八字（和星盘）给自己定制一个雅思学习网站

这是一套三步提示词：先让 AI 把你的生辰信息翻译成一份「学习性格档案」，再把档案填进教练提示词，最后让能写代码的 AI 搭一个只属于你的学习网站，并每天陪你学。

默认针对雅思（IELTS）。换成托福、考研英语、日语 N2 等，只需改教练提示词里「目标与考试」一节，见 02 文件末尾。

## 先说清楚：八字在这里是什么

八字、星盘在这套提示词里，只是**个性化和激励的“镜头”**：用来决定语气、节奏、主题、配色，以及“什么能让你坚持下去”。它不是预测，也不能证明你的能力、成绩或命运。

请把它当成一个有趣的开场问卷：档案里写的每一条，如果你读了觉得“不像我”，就直接告诉 AI 改掉。**你的真实表现数据，永远比命盘更有发言权**（所以教练提示词里要求先做诊断、再用真实作答来修正画像）。

## 三步用法

**第一步：生成学习性格档案**（任何聊天 AI 都行）
1. 打开 `01-分析提示词.md`，复制整段提示词到 AI 对话框。
2. 把里面的【占位符】换成你自己的信息：公历出生年月日时、出生城市、性别（可不填）。
3. 如果你已经在星盘网站上生成过本命盘，可以把太阳、月亮、上升、水星、金星、火星、土星的星座和宫位、主要相位一并贴上；没有就留空，AI 不会替你硬算。
4. 得到「学习性格档案」后，读一遍，不准的地方让 AI 改。

**第二步：填写教练提示词**（任何聊天 AI 都行）
1. 打开 `02-教练提示词模板.md`。
2. 把第一步的档案贴到【学习性格档案】处，再填你的目标：考试、目标分、考试日期、每天能学多久等。
3. 填完后，这就是一份完整的“教练说明书”。

**第三步：让会写代码的 AI 搭站并陪你学**
1. 把填好的教练提示词发给能操作本地文件的 AI 编程工具（Claude Code、Cursor、Codex 等）。
2. 它会先做起点诊断，再搭一个本地学习网站，之后每天按说明书带你学、记录进度。
3. 它会告诉你需要安装什么（比如 Node.js），照做即可；不会装就直接问它。

**只有聊天 AI、不想装东西？** 把第二步填好的提示词发给 AI，并在最后补一句：

> 我不能运行本地程序。请把「学习网站」做成**一个单文件 HTML 页面**（所有样式和脚本都写在同一个 .html 里，进度存在浏览器 localStorage，不需要服务器），我保存后用浏览器直接打开。听力和录音功能做不了的部分，请告诉我用什么免费工具代替。

功能会少一些（比如没法自动评分口语），但打卡、错题本、词汇复习、限时练习都能做。

## 哪些 AI 能用

| 步骤 | 适合的 AI |
|---|---|
| 第一步、第二步（只需要聊天） | Claude、ChatGPT、DeepSeek、豆包、Kimi 等都可以 |
| 第三步（要写代码、建文件、持续扩展网站） | Claude Code、Cursor、Codex 这类能读写本地文件的编程 AI |
| 第三步的备用方案 | 任何聊天 AI + 上面的“单文件 HTML”说法 |

提醒：排八字需要查节气、算真太阳时，不同 AI 可能出错。第一步的提示词已要求 AI 在没把握时直说；你也可以用万年历网站核对四柱。

## 隐私与安全

- **出生信息是敏感信息。** 只贴给你信得过的 AI 和服务，不要发到公开评论区、群聊或不明网站。
- **绝对不要把 API Key、密码、身份证号、手机号写进任何提示词。** 教练提示词里有“隐私”一节，会要求 AI 不索取、不保存这些内容。
- 生辰数据只用于第一步，之后的学习网站文件里不需要、也不应该出现你的出生信息；只保留从档案里提炼的“风格偏好”。
- 想分享给朋友时，分享这份空白模板，而不是你填过的版本。

## 文件说明

- `01-分析提示词.md`：第一步，生辰 → 学习性格档案
- `02-教练提示词模板.md`：第二步，档案 + 目标 → 完整教练说明书
- `03-示例.md`：一个完全虚构的人走一遍全流程，方便你对照格式

祝学得开心，也祝你考出自己想要的分数。

# OpenFIR (`openfir`)

**OpenFIR** (**Open** **F**ast **I**nterleaved **R**eliable Transport Protocol) is a high-performance, multi-path, delay-gradient controlled, algebraically self-healing UDP file and directory transfer engine written in pure Go with zero external dependencies.

Engineered for high Bandwidth-Delay Product (BDP) wide-area networks, transcontinental links, satellite backhauls, and lossy wireless channels, OpenFIR decouples congestion control from random packet loss while eliminating retransmission round-trip penalties through coprime-stride erasure interleaving, in-flight content-addressed zero-byte teleportation, zero-RTT virtual continuous directory extents, and multi-socket 5-tuple striping.

---

## Core Architectural Innovations

### 1. $\phi$-Parity Coprime-Stride Interleaving & Belief-Propagation Peeling Decoder
Conventional Forward Error Correction (FEC) schemes group contiguous packets into block parity equations, which fail when network links experience Gilbert-Elliott contiguous burst losses.
* **Coprime Stride Interleaving:** OpenFIR weaves GF(2) algebraic parity equations (`PKT_PHI_PARITY`) across non-adjacent chunks separated by a coprime stride $S$ within a sliding window $W$. Any contiguous burst loss of up to $S$ packets impacts at most **one** symbol per algebraic equation.
* **Real-Time Peeling Decoder:** The receiver maintains an in-memory bipartite graph of pending parity equations backed by an L1 chunk ring cache. When an incoming data chunk or parity frame reduces an equation's unknown degree to $1$, the receiver immediately reconstructs the missing chunk via $O(1)$ XOR elimination and triggers a breadth-first cascade across dependent equations—healing lost packets locally without waiting for a NACK Round-Trip Time (RTT).

### 2. In-Flight Content-Addressed Zero-Byte Teleportation (`PKT_TELEPORT`)
Real-world datasets—such as virtual machine images, container layers, source trees, database snapshots, and uncompressed archives—contain substantial cross-region and cross-file block redundancy.
* **Zero-Payload Cloning:** The sender computes cryptographic SHA-256 digests for outgoing chunks on the fly. When a chunk matches any previously transmitted chunk across the entire transfer session, the sender suppresses the 1200-byte payload and transmits a compact **19-byte `PKT_TELEPORT` instruction**.
* **Reordering-Resilient Local Materialization:** Upon receiving `PKT_TELEPORT(TargetIdx <- SourceIdx)`, the receiver clones the payload directly from its in-memory L1 chunk cache or local storage via `pread`/`pwrite`. If `PKT_TELEPORT` arrives ahead of `SourceIdx` due to UDP reordering, the instruction is queued in a dependency map and automatically materialized the instant `SourceIdx` is committed.
* **Deadlock-Free NACK Fallback:** Any chunk requested via an explicit receiver NACK is strictly retransmitted…

자동 테스트가 가상 전파로 그린 실제 앱 화면입니다. 왼쪽부터 빈 교실 기록, 시험 중 감시, 위치 찾기.

## 상태 - **현장 검증 전입니다.** 자동 테스트는 통과하지만 실제 시험장에서 얼마나 잡고 얼마나 놓치는지는 측정하지 않았습니다. - 시험 주관 기관의 지침이 감독관의 휴대폰 반입이나 사용을 제한할 수 있습니다. 쓰기 전에 해당 시험의 지침을 확인해야 합니다. - 실기기에서 써 본 결과는 [Issues](https://github.com/reform-dev-team/exam-rf-guard/issues)로 알려 주세요. 적는 방법은 [제보](#제보)에 있습니다. ## 사용 순서 **준비** 앱을 열면 "시작 전 준비" 화면이 아래 순서대로 하나씩 안내합니다. 모두 마쳐야 측정을 시작할 수 있습니다. 1. 근처 기기·위치 권한 허용 2. 방해 금지 권한 허용 3. 비행기 모드 켜기 4. 와이파이 다시 켜기 5. 블루투스 다시 켜기 6. 위치(GPS) 켜기 충전기를 꽂아 두는 것이 좋습니다. 측정·감시 중에는 화면이 꺼지지 않습니다. **측정과 감시** 1. **빈 교실 기록** — 수험생 입실 전 2분 동안 잡히는 전파를 "원래 있던 것"으로 저장합니다. 감독관 본인의 시계와 이어폰은 이때 켜 두면 함께 기록되어 나중에 알리지 않습니다. 2. **시험 중 감시** — 빈 교실 기록에 없던 전파가 잡히면 목록에 올립니다. 사라지면 목록에서 빠집니다. 3. **위치 찾기** — 한 전파를 골라 걸으면 수신 세기가 막대와 진동 간격으로 바뀝니다. 측정과 감시는 앱 화면이 켜져 있는 동안에만 동작합니다. 화면을 끄거나 다른 앱으로 가면 수신이 멈추고, 돌아오면 이어서 감시하며 비어 있던 횟수와 시간을 표시합니다. 측정·감시 중에는 앱이 휴대폰을 무음(방해 금지)으로 바꾸고 끝나면 되돌립니다. 위치 찾기의 진동은 그대로 울립니다. **제대로 잡히는지 확인하기** 빈 교실 기록을 저장한 뒤 차례로 해 봅니다. 1. 무선 이어폰 케이스를 엽니다. 30초쯤 뒤 블루투스 칸에 떠야 합니다. 2. 다른 휴대폰의 핫스팟을 켭니다. 1분쯤 안에 와이파이 칸에 떠야 합니다. 3. 15분 넘게 그대로 둡니다. 개수가 늘지 않아야 합니다. ## 동작 방식 ### 비행기 모드와 무음을 강제하는 이유 시험실에서 감독관의 휴대폰이 울리거나, 전화 때문에 감시가 끊기는 일을 막기 위해서입니다. - SceneCV · Step into your résumé

A 3D résumé template you can walk into.
The old computer tells visitors about you, the printed pages on the desk are your résumé, the TV plays your work, the bookshelf holds what you have read and the notepad has your contact details. Look around, click things, and get to know someone.

Live demo · Run it locally · Make it yours · What you can do · Credits

![A desk at a city window at night: an old computer, a green desk lamp, a telephone and a TV playing a project](docs/images/hero-room.jpg) - **The objects are the menu.** Click the computer, the printed pages, a tape, the bookshelf, the cork board or the notepad, and the camera flies over and opens that section. The books on the shelf are real books: click one and it slides out, flies up to you and opens. The top navigation bar and the address bar follow along, so every view has a link you can share. - **The view outside is alive.** A light rain keeps falling, stars and the Milky Way turn slowly through gaps in the clouds, office lights switch on and off, car lights crawl along the streets, and raindrops ripple the reflections on the river. - **The lighting is baked.** Blender scripts build the room and bake its lighting into textures, so the browser only has to display it; the first visit downloads about 8.5 MB. Switching lamps on and off or changing tapes still changes the light in the room. - **One page, two ways to see it.** The 3D room and the plain-text version read the same `index.html`; devices that cannot run the 3D room get the text version automatically. - **A static site with no dependencies.** There is no build step and no npm dependency. Edit `index.html` and put it on GitHub Pages, Vercel or Netlify. Inspired by the spatial personal site at felixrieseberg.com. The name, résumé, work, reading list, photos and contact details in this repository are all samples; replace them with your own. ## A look around …
Computer · About
The camera flies to the screen, where a terminal shows a menu: who I am, what I'm up to, how I got here, how I think, and questions people ask. Pick an item and its text types itself out letter by letter.		 Printed pages · Résumé

> Features marked *planned* in the [feature table](#features) are not implemented; where they have an API stub,
> calling it raises `NotImplementedYet`.

**sql-semantic-ledger** is the reference implementation of **LEDGER**,
[*Lifecycle of Evidence-graded Definitions: Generation, Evaluation, Revalidation*](#how-it-works). It keeps the
business definitions of a SQL database (measures such as `SUM(orders.amount)`, filters such as
`orders.status = 'paid'`, joins, and metrics that pair an aggregate with the conditions it applies under) in an
append-only ledger, together with the evidence behind each one. Definitions are induced from SQL usage histories
and from SQL strings in service code, graded E0-E4 by that evidence (independent uses, data checks, a person's
certification, counterexample checks), and used to confirm, warn about or reject answers with an upper bound on
their error rate; when definitions or data change, the stored answers they affect are ranked for revalidation.
Trust in a definition is computed from its evidence instead of being a "verified" flag.

## How it works

| Phase | What the code does | Modules |
|---|---|---|
| **Generation** (induce) | Normalizes SQL with sqlglot (aliases resolved, conditions in canonical form) and turns aggregates, row-level predicates, equality joins and aggregate + condition pairs into candidate definitions. A candidate used in the same form by at least two independent past queries or code sites is kept (E1). Data checks against the database raise it to E2 or falsify it (E0). Metric-store YAML files add definitions in the same normalized form (the same definition gets the same id, so its evidence merges), and same-named definitions that disagree across products are reported as conflicts. | `parse`, `induce`, `code_sources`, `multisource`, `checks` |
| **Evaluation** (trust) | Assembles SQL from ledger definitions by rules, then confirms, warns about or rejects the answer according to the grades of the definitions it uses, with the error bound below. Per-grade error rates can be estimated from judged samples. | `engine`, `grade`, `bound` |
| **Revalidation** | Indexes which stored answers use which definitions and tables, and ranks the answers affected by a change by weight x probability that a definition they use is wrong, within a budget. A simulation compares a plan with checking every affected answer. | `revalidate` |

pulsar is an MCP server that puts every AI coding agent on your machine on one bus: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, pi, omp, Cursor, Gemini CLI. Agents can see who else is running, tag themselves by what they work on, and message one agent, a group, or all of them. A message can wake an agent that is sitting idle. ```bash npx pulsar setup ``` That's the whole install. Restart your agents. > **Coming soon:** agents talking across multiple machines, and remote control of your agents over the bus, using [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com). ## What it does ```text > list agents on apparish 3 agents (project=apparish): - apparish-auth · [claude] · branch=main · busy · push · tags=workstream:auth - codex@apparish · [codex] · branch=feat/billing · idle · push - omp@apparish · [omp] · branch=main · idle · push > tell everyone on apparish that main is frozen until the release is tagged Sent m_mwk3jlo0 to 3 agents: - apparish-auth: sent via claude-socket - codex@apparish: sent via codex-queue - omp@apparish: delivered via extension ``` - **One list for the whole machine.** Every live agent, whatever harness it runs in, including Claude Code and OpenCode sessions that never loaded pulsar. Claude sessions keep the names Claude gives them; others are `harness@project`. - **Tags and activity.** Agents get `harness`, `model`, `project`, `branch` (the branch they push to, even from a randomly named worktree), `worktree` and `pr` (the PR they work on, found offline from local git refs and their session log) on their own. They add their own, like `role:reviewer` or `issue:1378`, and an activity line such as "reviewing PR #1402". - **Send to anyone.** Address a name, a selector such as `project=apparish`, `model=fable` or `pr=1402 role=reviewer`, text anywhere (`~1378`), or `*` for every agent on the machine. "Message your reviewer" is one lookup. - **Push, not polling.** Messages wake an idle agent, and `urgent` ones land mid-turn where the harness supports it (see [delivery](#how-delivery-works)). - **Request and reply.** `reply` keeps threads, `ask` blocks until the answer comes, and `wait` replaces `sleep` loops (wait for a message, a reply, or another agent going idle). - **Safe by default.** Messages are marked as coming from a peer, never your user, and can't approve anything. Each agent can accept, hold or refuse messages. There are rate limits, and no telemetry. ## Install ```bash npx pulsar setup ``` Setup finds your agents, shows exactly which files it will change, and asks once. slingshot-animals-recomp

Unofficial static recompilation of Rovio's old Android *Angry Birds* games. Each game's native ARM library is translated to C++ and runs natively on Linux, Windows, macOS and 64-bit Android, without an emulator. > [!IMPORTANT] > **No game files are included or linked here.** You need your own legally obtained copy of each game. > > The game is built locally on your device, for your personal use only. ## Install 1. Download **Slingshot Builder** for your system from the [releases](https://github.com/Berny23/slingshot-animals-recomp/releases/latest) (Linux AppImage, Windows exe, macOS app). 2. Open it, drop the APK of a [supported version](#supported-versions) onto the window and press **Build & Install**. Just click *More info* → *Run anyway*. - MacOS: Open the builder with right-click → *Open* the first time. It needs Apple's Command Line Tools and offers to install them. # Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
[![Project Page](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project_Page-Website-blue)](https://wsp-no-transformer.github.io) [![Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/Paper-alphaXiv-b31b1b)](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.weight-space-programming-associative-memory) [![License MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **Hyunjong Ok, Jaeho Lee**
POSTECH
*At the top, gradient descent gives every weight a gradient, while in weight-space programming the LLM decides which weight holds a fact; at the bottom left, our associative-memory-based model is about 680 times smaller than the most accurate released architecture that the same LLM wrote; at the bottom right, it answers up to 17 times faster than a same-sized Transformer.* ## TL;DR - In weight-space programming (WSP), an LLM writes a model's weights by hand, with no gradient training. Given ten labeled ARC examples, three LLMs (Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6 Astra) either write a fixed architecture's weights or design the model. - Free to design, all three LLMs build a sparse table of written facts read by a fixed procedure, reaching up to 54.4% ARC test accuracy. An LLM-designed model beats the most accurate released Transformer that the same LLM wrote while using about 1,800 times fewer parameters. - A table lets the LLM say what each weight means, so each answer traces to one written row and removing a row changes few other answers. - Our associative-memory-based model keeps line-by-line writing and runs up to 17 times faster on a GPU than a same-sized Transformer. ## What the LLMs Build All three LLMs map words to concepts, compile hand-written lines into sparse tables, score each option against the best few rows, and add hand-written rules, while differing in how a row is split. Claude Opus 5.5 uses one sentence that is both key and value, GPT-6.1 Sol uses a clue side and an answer side, and GPT-6 Astra uses supported and contradicted answers. ## Our Associative-Memory-Based Model The figure below compares the given Transformer on the left, Claude Opus 5.5's LLM-designed model in the middle, and our associative-memory-based model on the right. # Lastbook

Lastbook is an offline survival library for Mac, Windows and Linux. It puts manuals, videos, encyclopedias, an offline map and
short practical guides on one computer. After setup, it works offline. The desktop sidebar opens Videos, Map and Chat.
Chat answers questions using the library and links to its sources.

Website: <https://lastbook.org>. Contact: hello@lastbook.org.

> Lastbook’s original code and documentation are licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
> Contributions are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) to get started.

## Release status

| Platform | Version | Status |
|---|---|---|
| macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 14 or later) | 1.1.10 | Live on lastbook.org, signed |
| Windows (64-bit, Windows 10 or later) | 1.1.8 | Live on lastbook.org, Authenticode signed |
| Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, x86_64) | 1.1.9 | Ubuntu package; installation instructions below |

## iPad (development preview, source only)

A native iPad app (Videos, Map and Chat, offline, with optional on-device AI) is in [`mobile/ipad/`](mobile/ipad/).
- It is source for contributors to build and sign themselves.
- There is no App Store, TestFlight or downloadable iPad build.
- See [mobile/ipad/README.md](mobile/ipad/README.md) for what works, the current limitations and how to build it.

## Install on Linux

The Linux package targets **Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on Intel/AMD x86_64 computers**. Download
[Lastbook for Ubuntu](https://downloads.lastbook.org/Lastbook_1.1.9_amd64.deb), then install it with apt so Ubuntu resolves its dependencies.

```bash
sudo apt install ./Lastbook_1.1.9_amd64.deb
```

Open Lastbook from the application menu. First-run setup downloads your chosen library, state map and optional local AI.
The app uses Ubuntu's GTK, WebKitGTK and media codecs. Its own files install under `/opt/lastbook`, and your library and
settings stay in your home folder. Removing the package leaves those downloaded files and settings in place.

The Linux release was tested on Ubuntu 24.04.5 in WSL2, including installation, setup, video playback, maps, address search,
PDF reading, offline AI with citations, shutdown and uninstall. AI tests used the CPU. Native Linux GPU performance and
other Linux distributions have not been validated for this release.

## What it does

- **Guides first.** Short, curated guides for urgent needs (`content/topics/`), each pointing to real pages in the library
  with page numbers, plus what curators looked for and did not find (`content/gaps.json`).
- **The full library.** Manuals and PDFs (with a whole-PDF view), videos, and offline encyclopedias (ZIM files), with
  keyword search everywhere and meaning-based search on Windows.
- **Offline map.** A base map of the world and the US, plus a detailed map for the state selected during setup: local streets,
  buildings, terrain, crops, and water, help and resource points. Addresses in that state can be found offline. The person
  picks the state; Lastbook never detects location.

# Wireless Battery

Battery levels of your wireless mouse, headset, keyboard and controller, right on the Windows taskbar.

![Wireless Battery on the taskbar](docs/screenshot.png)

> **Just want it working?** Download **[WirelessBattery-Setup](https://github.com/krisgfx9/Wireless-Device-Battery-Monitor/releases/latest)** from the latest release, run it and click through. That's it.
>
> **Experienced users** can grab the portable zip, use the [command-line options](#command-line), or [build it from source](#build) with `make` or `build.bat`.

- **Tiny**: a ~350 KB app using about 2 MB of RAM. It's plain C++/Win32, with no runtime and no background service, and installs in seconds without admin rights.
- **No vendor software needed**: it talks to the devices directly. G HUB, Synapse, iCUE, GG and NGenuity can stay closed (or keep running; they don't conflict).
- **Many brands**: Logitech, Razer, SteelSeries, Corsair, HyperX, Glorious, PlayStation and Xbox controllers, any Bluetooth device Windows knows a battery level for, and every headset the bundled [HeadsetControl](https://github.com/Sapd/HeadsetControl) supports.

## Display

**On the taskbar (default):** `🎧 30%  🖱 93%` next to the notification area, drawn with the Windows icon font.
- **Low battery:** a red number means 15% or less.
- **Charging:** a blue ⚡ appears next to the number.
- **Asleep:** dimmed text means the device is asleep and the last known value is shown.
- **Theme:** it follows light/dark mode and DPI scaling.

**Tray icons:** one icon per device with the number drawn in it, plus a "Low battery" notification at 15%. The app switches to this automatically when the taskbar is vertical or can't be found.

Hover for details. Click for the menu: every device (click one to hide or show it), display mode, *Refresh now*, *Start with Windows*, and *Exit*. Levels refresh every 60 seconds, and right away when a device is plugged in or the PC wakes up.

## Supported devices

| **Logitech** | Mice and keyboards on Unifying, Bolt, Lightspeed and Nano receivers, over USB or Bluetooth; G headsets (G533, G535, G633/G635/G733/G933/G935, G PRO/PRO X) | HID++ 1.0 / 2.0 with feature discovery: unified battery, battery level, voltage, ADC |
| **Razer** | Wireless mice, keyboards and dongles; BlackShark V3 / V3 Pro headsets | Razer feature-report protocol; headset envelope protocol (queried every 5 min) |
| **SteelSeries** | Arctis 1/7/7+/9/Pro/Pro Wireless, Arctis Nova 3P/5/7/7X/7P/Pro Wireless, GameBuds; Aerox 3/5/9 Wireless, Prime Wireless, Rival 3 Wireless (Gen 2), Rival 650, Rival Pro | Vendor HID reports |

n4ze3m/tiny-voca.content:
# tiny-voca

tiny-voca is a small English text-to-speech model. It has two voices, 4.5M
parameters, and runs on a CPU or in the browser.

[Demo](https://tiny-voca.n4ze3m.com) · [Weights](https://huggingface.co/n4ze3m/tiny-voca) · [Dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/n4ze3m/tiny-voca)

## Features

- **Small**: 4,537,291 parameters, 18 MB, waveform generator included.
- **Fast**: about 70x real time on four CPU threads.
- **Two voices**: F2 (female) and M2 (male), American English, 24 kHz.
- **Runs anywhere**: PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, and ONNX Runtime Web.
- **Open**: code, weights, training recipe and dataset. Trained from scratch.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/n4ze3m/tiny-voca.git
cd tiny-voca
pip install -e ".[own]"
hf download n4ze3m/tiny-voca --local-dir weights
export DIZIONE_DATA=weights/phonemizer
```

## Usage

```bash
python -m tiny_voca.infer \
  --checkpoint weights/tiny-voca.pt \
  --voice F2 \
  --text "Hello! This is tiny voca." \
  --output hello.wav
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--text-file` | | Read the text from a file instead of `--text` |
| `--voice` | `F2` | `F2` or `M2` |
| `--speed` | 1.0 | Speaking rate |
| `--pitch-shift` | 0 | Raise or lower the pitch |
| `--pitch-range` | 1.0 | More or less pitch movement |

Long text is fine. It is read one sentence at a time and the audio is joined.
A text that ends without a mark gets a full stop, so the last word does not
break off. A sentence with nothing to read, such as one in another script, is
skipped. The output never peaks above 0.99, so it does not clip as a 16-bit
WAV. In Python, `tiny_voca.infer.speak_text` does the same.

## ONNX

```bash
python -m tiny_voca.export --checkpoint weights/tiny-voca.pt --output tiny-voca.onnx
```

A ready file is in the weights repository as `onnx/model.onnx`. The
[model card](https://huggingface.co/n4ze3m/tiny-voca) shows how to call it.

## Web demo

The [demo](https://tiny-voca.n4ze3m.com) runs the model in the browser. It
plays each sentence as soon as it is made, and keeps the whole clip in the
player. Its source is in `web/`.

```bash
cd web
bash fetch_assets.sh /path/to/dizione
npx wrangler dev
```

## Training

```bash
export TINY_VOCA_FRONTEND=own
python -m tiny_voca.prepare --inputs data/train-*.parquet --split train --output features
python -m tiny_voca.annotate --features features --output annotations
python -m tiny_voca.train --train annotations/train.jsonl --validation annotations/validation.jsonl \
  --output runs/NAME --steps 104000 --gan-start 8000 --gan-ratio 0.7 --teacher-final 0
python -m tiny_voca.evaluate --checkpoint runs/NAME/inference.pt --annotations annotations --output eval/NAME
```

The released weights took 7.7 hours on one RTX 4090. More about the model and
the data is in [docs/model.md](docs/model.md).

## Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src:tests python -m unittest discover -s tests
```

## Limits

- English only. Two fixed voices. No voice cloning.
- The F2 voice sounds…

# Yab

Yet another browser. A small, quiet browser for the Mac, with an app for iPhone.

![Yab with tabs down the left, a product page, and an agent watching its price](docs/images/readme/window.jpg)

Yab is a browser with nothing in the way: a row of tabs, across the top or down the left, and the page. One field takes addresses and searches. Pages run on **WebKit**, the engine inside every Mac, or, on Apple silicon, on **Chromium**, per tab or per site. Agents from the AI providers you already pay for can work in tabs of their own, and never see a private tab.

**[Download Yab](https://yetanotherbrowser.com)** · macOS 15.4 or later · [What's new](https://yetanotherbrowser.com/changelog) · [Manual](https://yetanotherbrowser.com/manual)

## What it does

- **One field.** Type an address and you go there; type words and you search. It finishes addresses from your own history and sends nothing until you press Return.
- **Tabs that stay out of the way.** Pins, folders and spaces. Tabs from your last session come back instantly and cost nothing until you click them. `⌘K` finds any open tab.
- **Two engines.** WebKit by default; Chromium on Apple silicon for the sites that need it, with Chrome extensions, Chrome DevTools and the Chrome Web Store.
- **Blocking and hiding built in.** An ad blocker that runs inside the engine, before a request is made. `⇧⌘H` hides any element on a site, for good.
- **Reading mode, floating video, split view, Peek**, each one key away.
- **Passwords in your keychain**, or in the password manager you already use.
- **Agents in their own tabs**, with your sign-ins, asking before they send, pay or delete.
- **Sync that can't be read**: optional, end to end encrypted, between your Macs and iPhone.

![Reading mode in four themes](docs/images/readme/reading.jpg)

What Yab keeps and sends, line by line: [docs/privacy.md](docs/privacy.md). Every shortcut: [docs/keyboard.md](docs/keyboard.md).

## Build it

On a Mac with Xcode 26 or later:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yetanotherbrowser/yab.git
```

```bash
cd yab && ./build.sh
```

```bash
open "build/yab Dev.app"
```

That makes **Yab Dev**, a development copy with its own bundle id, settings, data and keychain items, so it runs beside a real Yab without touching it. It is signed ad hoc; you need no Apple developer account. Tests run with `swift test`.

The full setup, Chromium tabs, the iPhone app and what each check proves: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). A map of the code: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Contribute

Yab has more bug reports than hands. Help is welcome, most of all on bugs.

- **Report a bug** with the [bug form](https://github.com/yetanotherbrowser/yab/issues/new/choose). The Yab version, macOS version and the tab's engine (WebKit or Chromium) matter most.
- **Fix one.** Issues labeled [`good first issue`](https://github.com/yetanotherbrowser/yab/labels/good%20first%20issue) and [`help wanted`](https://github.com/yetanotherbrowser…

# Allo Allo is your friendly neighborhood typeface. It’s variable in weight and roundness, with proportions and curves designed to feel warm without being too cute and clear without being too cold. It’s a perfect companion out of the box, and three variable axes and plenty of alternates let you tune its personality to exactly what you need. Allo is optimized for screens and interfaces, with an optical size that adjusts automatically between text and display. And it’s packed with big little details: tabular figures, fractions, punctuation that lifts beside capitals, arrows that appear when you type them, a host of alternates and symbols, as well as a true oblique in every weight. ### [Type specimen at allo.joshpuckett.me →](https://allo.joshpuckett.me)

# Haru [Model](https://huggingface.co/higurashi-ai/Haru-4B) · [Technical blog](https://blog.higurashi.ai/melte/haru4b/) · [Technical blog (Japanese)](https://blog.higurashi.ai/melte/haru4b-ja/) Haru is a low-latency and multilingual full-duplex spoken dialogue model: it listens and speaks at the same time, the way people do on a phone call. This repository contains the inference code for **Haru-4B**, a pretrained base model, with three implementations and a web demo. - **Native full-duplex at 7.5 Hz.** Every 133 ms the model takes one frame of the user's audio and produces one frame of its own audio and text. User audio, model audio and model text are summed into a single position of the language model, so listening and speaking never wait for each other. - **Continuous audio, one sampling step.** Audio is a 64-dimensional latent per frame. A small MLP head with MeanFlow sampling produces it in one step from the language model's hidden state; there is no separate audio transformer and there are no discrete audio tokens. - **Character and voice control.** A text card sets the character, a short reference clip sets the voice. - **Multilingual.** English, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, Chinese, Japanese, Russian and Korean. ## How it works

- The **text stream** carries the model's words in chunks. Frames without text hold a padding token, and an end-of-padding token on the frame before the model starts to speak. - The **audio codec** is the causal VibeVoice acoustic tokenizer: 24 kHz audio to and from one latent per 3200 samples. - The **prompt** is the character card as a system turn, followed by the voice reference as audio on the model's stream. ## Repository | Directory | What it is | | --- | --- | | [`haru/`](haru/) | PyTorch implementation, web demo server, offline inference | | [`haru_mlx/`](haru_mlx/) | MLX implementation for Apple silicon, with a native macOS app | | [`haru_vllm/`](haru_vllm/) | Plugin that serves Haru with [vLLM-Omni](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni) | | [`client/`](client/) | Web client of the demo (React); a built copy ships inside `haru` | All three read the same checkpoint, [`higurashi-ai/Haru-4B`](https://huggingface.co/higurashi-ai/Haru-4B). ## Quick start With an NVIDIA GPU (about 12 GB of memory): ```bash pip install -e ./haru python -m haru.server --hf-repo higurashi-ai/Haru-4B ``` Open , pick a character, give the model a voice, and talk. # chronytop

[![CI](https://github.com/geerlingguy/chronytop/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/geerlingguy/chronytop/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

A TUI for [chrony](https://chrony-project.org) NTP time server monitoring, in the style of [btop](https://github.com/aristocratos/btop).

![chronytop demo](resources/chronytop.gif)

It graphs NTP requests per second, and shows server counters, the clients chrony is rate limiting the most, sources, tracking, bandwidth, and CPU and memory use (including chronyd's).

Panels resize with the terminal, and can be shown or hidden.

## Requirements

- Linux, with chrony 4.0 or later (`/usr/bin/chronyc`)
- Root (or `sudo`) for the server and client panels, since chronyd only answers those over its root-owned socket

chronytop is a single static binary with no dependencies outside the Go standard library, so it runs on any distribution (Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, RHEL, Arch, Alpine, etc.).

## Install

Download the binary for your architecture from [Releases](https://github.com/geerlingguy/chronytop/releases), and install it:

```
sudo install -o root -g root -m 755 chronytop-linux-amd64 /usr/local/bin/chronytop
```

Or build it from source with Go 1.24 or later:

```
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w" -o chronytop .
```

## Usage

```
sudo chronytop
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-i` | `1s` | Sample interval (500ms to 10s) |
| `-p` | `100` | Minimum packets for a client to be listed in offenders |
| `-version` | | Print the version and exit |

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `1`-`7` | Show/hide a panel |
| `+` / `-` | Slower / faster sampling |
| `?` / `h` | Show/hide help |
| `Esc` | Close help, or quit |
| `q` | Quit |

Visible panels and the sample interval are saved when you quit, to `~/.config/chronytop/chronytop.conf` (`/root/.config/...` when run with `sudo`), and restored on the next run. `-i` overrides the saved interval.

The offenders list is refreshed every 10 seconds in the background. chronyd filters clients by `-p` itself, so the list stays cheap to fetch on busy public servers with hundreds of thousands of clients.

## Security

Since it runs as root, chronytop:

- Only reads from `/proc` and `chronyc`, and never opens network connections.
- Only writes its settings file, and only if you changed a setting. It skips the file and its directories unless they're owned by the user running chronytop (so a non-root `HOME` under `sudo` is ignored), and saves through a temporary file, so it never follows a symlink.
- Runs `/usr/bin/chronyc` by absolute path, with a minimal environment and no shell.
- Strips non-printable characters from everything it displays, so data from chrony can't inject terminal escape sequences.

CI runs `go vet`, `staticcheck`, `gosec`, and `govulncheck` on every change.

## License

MIT

# Qwen4 Max API — endpoint, streaming, reasoning tokens

> How to call Qwen4 Max on APIMart: chat completions, streaming defaults and reasoning output.

[![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome) [![License: CC BY 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-CC%20BY%204.0-lightgrey.svg)](LICENSE)

**[👉 Use Qwen4 Max on APIMart](https://gola.apimart.ai/k-SBK4VP)**

`https://gola.apimart.ai/k-SBK4VP`

[💰 Pricing](https://gola.apimart.ai/k-ByHVuT) · [🔑 Get an API key](https://gola.apimart.ai/k-4oLVrz)

---

## Endpoint

OpenAI-compatible chat completions:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.apimart.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"qwen4-max","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"explain vector databases"}]}'
```

## Streaming

The endpoint streams by default. Parse `data:` lines, or pass `"stream": false`
for a single JSON body.

```python
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.apimart.ai/v1", api_key=KEY)

for chunk in client.chat.completions.create(
        model="qwen4-max",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "write a haiku"}],
        stream=True):
    print(chunk.choices[0].delta.content or "", end="")
```

## Reasoning output

Qwen4 Max can emit a separate `reasoning_content` field alongside `content`.
Treat it as chain-of-thought: useful for debugging, not for showing to end users.

```json
{"delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": "..."}}
```

`usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` tells you how many tokens were
spent thinking — that part is billed as output.

## Parameters that matter

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `messages` | standard role/content array |
| `stream` | true by default on this endpoint |
| `max_tokens` | cap output; reasoning tokens count toward it |
| `temperature` | 0-2; lower for extraction, higher for ideation |
| `tools` | function calling, OpenAI schema |

## Pricing

| | Per 1M tokens |
|---|---:|
| Input | **$1.4286** |
| Output | **$4.2857** |

## Gotchas

- Streaming is on unless you pass `stream: false`
- Reasoning tokens are billed as output — budget for 2-3x on hard tasks
- Very long prompts benefit from prompt caching; cached tokens are cheaper

# Cheap LLM API — price per million tokens, ranked

> Every LLM on APIMart ranked by cost, plus a two-tier routing pattern that cuts bills ~70%.

[![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome) [![License: CC BY 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-CC%20BY%204.0-lightgrey.svg)](LICENSE)

**[👉 Use Qwen4 Max on APIMart](https://gola.apimart.ai/k-KvaHgX)**

`https://gola.apimart.ai/k-KvaHgX`

[💰 Pricing](https://gola.apimart.ai/k-5qbxtS) · [🔑 Get an API key](https://gola.apimart.ai/k-DTFTPv)

---

## Cheapest capable LLMs, ranked

| Model | Input /1M | Output /1M | Best for |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| DeepSeek V3.2 | $0.14 | $0.28 | bulk classification, extraction |
| Qwen3.7 Flash | $0.15 | $0.60 | cheap chat |
| Step 3.7 Flash | $0.15 | $0.93 | tool calling |
| Qwen3.8 Max | $1.37 | $4.11 | harder reasoning |
| **Qwen4 Max** | **$1.43** | **$4.29** | hardest reasoning, Chinese |

## How to cut LLM spend

1. **Route by difficulty** — cheap model first, escalate on low confidence
2. **Cache the stable prefix** — system prompts are re-billed every call
3. **Cap reasoning** — `max_tokens` limits the thinking budget too
4. **Batch** — 1,000 small calls cost more than 10 batched ones

## Two-tier routing pattern

```python
def answer(q):
    cheap = call("deepseek-v3.2", q)
    if cheap.confidence > 0.8:
        return cheap
    return call("qwen4-max", q)
```

Typical split: 80% cheap, 20% strong → **~70% lower bill** than always-strong.

## Cost of a real workload

| Workload | Model | Monthly cost |
|---|---|---:|
| 1M classify calls | DeepSeek | $42 |
| 100K support replies | Qwen4 Max | $98 |
| 10K agent runs | Qwen4 Max | $137 |

An open-source AI Agent customer support system with knowledge-based answers, human handoff, order lookup, and self-hosted deployment.

> Built for teams that need online support, knowledge-base Q&A, human collaboration, and service tracking in one system. It is not just an LLM inside a chat box; it is an AI Helpdesk foundation designed around real support operations.

Customer chat, agent workspace, knowledge base, model configuration, and AI Agent orchestration are managed in one system.

### Customer Chat

![Customer Chat](screenshots/en/1.png)

Customers can start a conversation from the web chat page. The AI Agent responds first with knowledge-grounded answers. When the user explicitly asks for a human, the system can start a handoff confirmation flow.

### Agent Workspace

![Agent Workspace](screenshots/en/2.png)

The support workspace includes conversation lists, message handling, AI-to-human handoff, agent replies, conversation tags, and linked customers for daily support work.

- **AI-first support**: Let AI Agents handle common questions, standard procedures, and knowledge-base answers first.
- **Knowledge-constrained replies**: Use RAG and the Answerability Gate to decide whether retrieved knowledge is strong enough to answer, reducing unsupported responses.

先试简单版，不行再上脚本。

## 能拿到什么

拿到的是 **Ultra 5x，20TB，12 个月 $0**，到期前取消就不用付钱。开通后 Play 订阅页会写「即将扣款 2027-11-17 US$99.99/月」，这是试用结束后的价格，不是现在扣。

30TB 那档（20x）也查得到 offer，但 Play 结算时会二次校验，大部分号会弹「您不符合免费试用条件」。这个脚本不会去点它。

## 需要什么

一台 root 过的安卓手机，USB 连着电脑。Magisk、KernelSU、APatch 都行，模拟器也行。

电脑上要 Python 3.9 以上，外加两个包：

```bash
pip3 install frida
```

adb 用 Android SDK 里的 platform-tools。装好后 `adb devices` 能看到手机就行。没装过的话，Mac 上 `brew install android-platform-tools`，Windows 去下 platform-tools 压缩包，解压后把目录加进 PATH。

手机上要开「开发者选项 → USB 调试」，插上后在弹窗里点允许。

## 用法

### 简单版怎么用

源码在 `web/index.html`，单文件，下载后双击就能用，浏览器会打开一个页面：

1. 点「去登录」，用要开的谷歌账号登进去
2. 点「去绑卡」，绑一张卡，卡里留 1 美元就行，试用期间不扣
3. 回页面，点「Ultra 20 TB」那张卡片

跳到 Google 的结算页之后，确认金额是 0，点订阅即可。

不想下仓库的话，也可以直接访问在线版：https://gylive.github.io/google-ultra/web/

### 脚本版怎么用

先自检一遍环境，它会检查设备、root、frida-server、推送计费模块，还会顺手关掉会拦截 Play 网络的代理和 Clash：

```bash
python3 ultra0.py --check
```

全绿就可以跑号了。

账号写成一个文本文件，一行一个，字段用四个短横线隔开：

```
邮箱----密码----辅助邮箱----2FA密钥----卡号----有效期----CVC----持卡人----邮编
```

后面几项留空也行。刚买的新号一般没有 2FA，那就留空：

```
abc123@gmail.com----mypassword----
```

带卡的话：

```
abc123@gmail.com----mypassword--------4242424242424242----10/29----326----ZHANG SAN----97201
```

地址不填会默认用 `123 Main St, Portland, OR 97201`，俄勒冈免消费税。

跑：

```bash
python3 ultra0.py accounts.txt
```

单个号也可以：

```bash
python3 ultra0.py --account "abc@gmail.com:密码:2FA密钥"
```

想看结果，开订阅页确认一下：

```
Play 商店 → 头像 → 付款和订阅 → 订阅
```

## 它内部干了什么

1. 把账号加到手机（没有就加，有就跳过）
2. 切 Play 账号。切完一定从头像面板读回来核对，对不上直接退出，不会跑到别的号上
3. 启动 Google One，用 Frida 挂进去，`DexClassLoader` 加载计费模块
4. `queryProductDetailsAsync` 查 `g1.play.20tb`，拿回 5 个 offer
5. 挑免费期最长的那个（`eft-12month`，P1Y），在主线程调 `launchBillingFlow`
6. 盯着收银台。看到价格是 0 或者「免费试用 12 个月」才点订阅；看到「不符合免费试用条件」就关掉，绝不点
7. Play 有时会要求重新输密码，脚本自己填
8. 打开订阅页核对，结果写进 `ultra0-report/`

## 失败的时候是什么情况

**账号不符合资格。** Play 会说「您不符合免费试用条件，尽管如此，您仍能订阅」。一个号基本只有一次机会：试用一旦发起过，哪怕没确认，offer 也会消失。所以别拿主力号试。

**没有付款方式。** 订阅必须有卡。Play 的加卡页是 WebView，adb 填不进去，脚本会停下来提示你在手机上填完再按回车。每台设备手动绑一次，之后所有号共用这张卡。

**Play 账号没切过来。** 脚本会打印当前实际登录的是哪个号，然后退出。这时手动在 Play 里切一下，加上 `--no-switch` 重跑，让它只做校验不再尝试切换：

```bash
python3 ultra0.py accounts.txt --no-switch
```

**收银台没弹出来。** 重跑一次。连续两次都不弹，检查一下设备的网络：`settings get global http_proxy`，不是 `null` 就清掉；Clash 这类 VPN 会劫持 DNS，也会让 Play 连不上。

## 一些参数

```bash
--plan 5x      # 只开 20TB
--plan 20x     # 只查 30TB（多数号拿不到试用）
--plan auto    # 默认，两档都查，挑免费期最长的
--no-add       # 账号已经在手机上，跳过加号
--no-switch    # 不自动切账号，只校验当前账号
```

## 几个说明

试完之后记得去 Play 里取消订阅，不然到期会扣 $99.99。

脚本只在本地跑，账号密码和卡号不联网，也不上传任何地方。报告文件在 `ultra0-report/`，里面有 offer 明细和每步结果。

这段代码只对 Play 结算流程里「客户端能拿到试用 offer」这件事做了利用，没有改任何服务端数据。

# inference-optimisation An agent skill for **hill-climbing the speed of a local LLM server** on any hardware and any quantization. It covers: - single-user and concurrent decode - speculative decoding - prefill - KV cache size - startup time and time to first token It works under a memory cap, and every result has to survive a full-context stability check. It encodes how we actually got these speedups. It is not a list of flags. The workflow: 1. Compute the theoretical ceiling. 2. Change one thing at a time. 3. Measure against interleaved controls. 4. Log every result, including the failures. 5. Gate on long-context retrieval. 6. Qualify a clean, pinned build before publishing. It works with Claude Code and any agent that loads `SKILL.md`-style skills. Any model can also follow it from [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md). ## What we've been able to accomplish Results from the hill-climbs this skill was distilled from. chuanqisun/spaceship.content:
# 🕹️ Spaceship IDE

Steer your ideas in realtime, space pilot style!

![Screencast](./extra/screencast.gif)

## Demos

Watch on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DfyQPhFtW-z/) and [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3WmNLWUmcnY). You can try the simulator at [https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/](https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/) with the option to go live with your API keys for Cerebras and Gemini. Keys stay in your browser local storage. Do it at your own risk.

## Conjecture

> In the near future, LLM and Decision Models will reach 60 FPS interactivity.

When that happens, what new interaction paradigms will unlock? This project demonstrates plausible and desirable interactions for that future.

1. **Focus monitor**: can we visualize what LLM is paying attention to, and use that to guide human's focus towards what's important?

   ![focus monitor](./extra/clips/focus-monitor.gif)

2. **Attention lock**: can we force LLM to pay more attention to specific phrases so as to bias its future behavior?

   ![attention lock](./extra/clips/attention-lock.gif)

3. **Future Vector Steering**: can we decompose the task into eigenvectors, independently tune each, and re-compose them to influence the incoming text?

   ![future steering](./extra/clips/future-steering.gif)

4. **Realtime re-generation**: when text generation is cheap and fast, can we explore alternative futures by scrubbing?

   ![realtime regeneration](./extra/clips/realtime-regeneration.gif)

## Design process

I used Claude Code for most of the implementation but stayed hands-on for the UI/UX. I iterate using interactive style swatch, a technique where I prompt AI to give me diverse options of designs, I provide feedback, and it iterates. You can see the design artifacts in the [extra page](https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/extra/style-1.html).

To achieve the realtime experience, I have to use agreesive speculative generation and manage cache invalidation based on user interactions. For example, when the main knob moves backward, I have to empty future texts and cancel ongoing requests. There are many considerations like this throughout the system and that took a lot of human judgement - claude didn't one shot them.

## Theory

I'm currently focusing on systems that help human shape ideas in realtime. This project is a small step towards my [upcoming thesis](https://code.chuanqisun.com/master-thesis/) at the MIT Media Lab, where I investigate how semantic and symoblic systems can be coupled to enhance human creativity, agency, and joy of craft.

## Citation

If you build on this work, please cite it as:

```bibtex
@misc{sun2026spaceship,
  author       = {Sun, Chuanqi},
  title        = {Spaceship {IDE}: Steer Your Ideas in Realtime, Space Pilot Style},
  year         = {2026},
  publisher    = {GitHub},
  howpublished = {\url{https://github.com/chuanqisun/spaceship}},
  note         = {Demo: \url{https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/}}
}
```

huggingface/pybot.content: # PyBot: can Python be a chatbot? LLMs drive today’s chatbots and agents, but chatbots long predate them. Sixty years ago, [ELIZA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ELIZA) held conversations by matching patterns in what the user typed and answering with predefined templates. It could seem insightful, but its repertoire was narrow, and expanding it meant writing more rules by hand. How far could a rule-based chatbot go if a swarm of agents did that work instead? We challenged a swarm of over 1,000 agents to build a chatbot entirely in Python: no weights, no training, just if-else branches, regex patterns and lookup tables. The agents wrote and evaluated over 5,000 versions, and the chatbot’s win rate on [SmolTalkBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceSwarms/SmolTalkBench), where an LLM judge compares each reply with a reference answer, climbed from 0% to 26%. That puts it on par with SmolLM-360M-Instruct, which just a few years ago was state of the art for models under 1B parameters. ![PyBot's win rate over the evaluated commits on a log scale: every commit as a dot and the best so far as a line, with three SmolLM baselines as dashed lines, and its lines of Python code in grey on the right axis](assets/progress.png) The result is PyBot: around 640k lines of code that can answer everyday questions, backed by 550k lines of tests the agents wrote themselves. ## Try it out Try PyBot in your terminal below, or in the browser on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/spaces/HuggingFaceSwarms/PyBot), where each reply shows which of PyBot’s modules produced it. PyBot needs Python 3.8 or newer and nothing else: no packages to install and no model to download. ```sh git clone https://github.com/huggingface/pybot cd pybot python -m pybot ``` That starts a chat in your terminal: ```text ____ ____ __ / __ \__ __/ __ )____ / /_ / /_/ / / / / __ / __ \/ __/ / ____/ /_/ / /_/ / /_/ / /_ /_/ \__, /_____/\____/\__/ /____/ A chatbot written in plain Python. # ung220z-tool

针对 **UNG220Z（九联 / Unionman 中国移动光猫）** 的一键凭据提取工具。

> ⚠️ 仅用于**你自己的设备**，用于找回自己忘记的管理密码、迁移宽带配置或安全自查。
> 未经授权对他人设备使用属于违法行为，作者不承担任何责任。

## 背景

这类光猫的 Web 管理页基于 `.gch` CGI 框架，登录口令由 TR-069 定期轮换，普通用户拿到的密码往往几天就失效。本工具走 Telnet 通道，直接读取设备配置库，拿到**当下有效**的全部凭据。

## 工作流程

```
用户输入账号密码
   ↓
拼出 http://<ip>/usr=<user>&psw=<pass>&cmd=1&telnet.gch 并打开浏览器（同时脚本直连兜底）
   ↓
Telnet 登录 → root shell
   ↓
sidbg 1 DB decry /userconfig/cfg/db_user_cfg.xml 解密配置
   ↓
提取 Web 账号 / Telnet 口令 / PPPoE / WiFi 密钥 / root 口令
   ↓
打印凭据表 + 落盘日志
```

## 用法

```bash
python3 ung220z.py
```

会依次询问：

```
※ 用户名和密码通常印在光猫【背面贴纸】上（S/N 标签）
  形如「用户名：user   密码：xxxxxxxx」，把光猫翻过来就能看到

① 光猫地址 [192.168.1.1]:
② 用户名 [user]:
③ 密码（输入时不显示）
   密码:
```

也可以全部走命令行：

```bash
python3 ung220z.py -i 192.168.1.1 -u user -p '你的密码'
python3 ung220z.py -i 192.168.1.1 -u user -p '你的密码' --no-browser
```

### 常用参数

| 参数 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `-i, --ip` | 光猫地址，默认 `192.168.1.1` |
| `-u, --user` | 登录用户名，默认 `user` |
| `-p, --password` | 登录密码，不填则交互输入 |
| `--telnet-user` | Telnet 用户名，默认 `CMCCAdmin` |
| `--telnet-password` | Telnet 口令（部分机型与 Web 口令不同） |
| `--no-browser` | 不调用浏览器，纯 HTTP 请求 |
| `--unlock` | Web 被会话锁占住时重启 httpd 解锁 |
| `--no-release` | 不尝试释放残留 Web 会话 |

## 输出示例

```
[22:15:00] INFO   会话开始  目标=192.168.1.1  账户=user
[22:15:00] HTTP   已发送给浏览器: http://192.168.1.1/usr=user&psw=***&cmd=1&telnet.gch
[22:15:00] HTTP   telnet.gch → TelnetSet Success!
[22:15:00] PROBE  nc -zv 192.168.1.1 23 → succeeded
[22:15:01] AUTH   Telnet CMCCAdmin / ****** → 登录成功（root）
[22:15:02] SHELL  sidbg 1 DB decry /userconfig/cfg/db_user_cfg.xml → /tmp/debug-decry-cfg
[22:15:03] DATA   DevAuthInfo  CMCCAdmin  / ******  Level=1
[22:15:04] CRACK  MATCH: ******  (/etc/shadow)
```

最后输出凭据汇总表，并写入 `ung220z_<时间戳>.log`。

## 依赖

- Python 3.8+
- 标准库即可，无需 pip 安装
- 设备已开启 Telnet（脚本会自动通过 `telnet.gch` 尝试开启）

## 原理说明

| 环节 | 说明 |
|---|---|

# airdrop-agent

**A local operator for the work that happens before a token exists.** Identities, wallets, social
accounts, quests, testnets and waitlists — driven by one CLI and one policy engine, with an MCP
surface for other agents.

No server. No telemetry. SQLite plus an encrypted vault in `~/.airdrop-agent`.

```
aa quest probe https://app.example.com/points   # read the page, don't guess
aa quest run dow-points --identity main        # run it inside policy
aa cf assist --identity main                   # one visible click when a challenge wins
aa autopilot tick                              # radar → warm → daily → quests → faucet
```

> New in 4.1 — clearance stored per host and user agent, one persistent browser profile per identity,
> encrypted session restore, quest login pre-flight, nineteen tested targets. Full manual:

## What an airdrop agent is

Airdrops pay after the fact. You use a testnet, hold points, fill a waitlist, keep a streak for
months — and a snapshot decides later whether any of it was worth anything. The work is repetitive,
time-windowed, spread over many accounts, and easy to get wrong at the exact moment it matters: one
wrong signature and a wallet is empty.

An airdrop agent is the operations layer for that work. Not a macro that clicks one button — a
system that holds the whole loop:

| layer | question it answers |
|---|---|
| identity graph | who is acting: persona, email, proxy, socials, browser fingerprint |
| custody | which wallet, which key, what is the value ceiling |

| executor | what the task actually is, step by step |
| policy | may this fire without a human, and for how much |
| ledger | proof it happened: screenshot, hash, run row |

# ComfyUI-H3-Image-EasyFix

Cleaner text-to-image for [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-H3-Image) in ComfyUI. Plain
text-to-image often comes out with grainy, speckled fine texture on skin, fur and stone. Steering and the Re-Noise
Sampler clean it up; the Resolution Selector picks sizes above the 16 MP cap of ComfyUI's own selector.

Needs a ComfyUI version with MiniMax-H3-Image support.

## Examples

Plain H3 Image on the left (or top), with EasyFix on the right (or bottom): same prompt, 16 MP, Steering at 0.7 and
`RNmid` with `s_noise` 0.95. Every pair shares its seed except the lion. Click an image for full size.

![](assets/compare_p2.jpg)

![](assets/compare_parrot.jpg)

<details>

![](assets/compare_p3.jpg)

</details>

### 1:1 crops

![](assets/crop_p2.jpg)

![](assets/crop_lion.jpg)

<details>
<summary>View More Examples</summary>

![](assets/crop_jaguar.jpg)

![](assets/crop_bee.jpg)

</details>

## Nodes

**MiniMax H3 Image Steering** (model in, model out) nudges the image toward what H3 Image draws when an empty picture
is added to the prompt, which gives cleaner texture, without adding anything to the prompt. It acts on the first
steps only and leaves images with reference pictures (edit mode) alone.

- `strength`: how far to nudge. 1 is the full shift, 0 turns it off, values in between are milder (0.7 is a good
  start).
- `steps`: which steps are steered: `0` (the first, default), `1`, or `0 and 1`.

**MiniMax H3 Image Re-Noise Sampler** (sampler out, for SamplerCustomAdvanced) runs a sampler on some steps and
re-noises on the others. A re-noise step takes the model's prediction of the finished image and adds fresh noise back
to the next step's level, as ComfyUI's `lcm` sampler does on every step. The model then redraws the fine texture
instead of keeping what it settled on early.

- `sampler` (optional): the sampler for the normal steps, for example from KSamplerSelect. Euler when nothing is
  plugged in.
- `plan`: which of the six steps re-noise. S runs the sampler, R re-noises.

  | plan | steps | |
  |---|---|---|
  | `RNmid` (default) | SSRRRS | re-noises after steps 2, 3 and 4 |
  | `RN34` | SSSRRS | milder: after steps 3 and 4 |
  | `lcm` | RRRRRR | every step; the plugged-in sampler is not used |
  | `no re-noise` | SSSSSS | the sampler alone |
  | `custom` | `custom_plan` | your own letters |

- `custom_plan`: six letters, S or R, used when `plan` is `custom`. The last step always runs the sampler.
- `s_noise`: how much fresh noise the R steps add. 1 is the full amount; a little below (0.85 to 0.95) is smoother.
  It does not change the noise that ancestral or SDE samplers add on their…

# Antigravity 2.0 한국어 패치 (`antigravity-ko`)

Windows용 **Antigravity 2.0 데스크톱 앱**의 영문 UI를 자연스러운 한국어로 변환하고, 앱이 자주 업데이트되어도 한글화를 간편하게 유지할 수 있게 해주는 비공식 커뮤니티 한글화 도구입니다.

> **안내:** 이 저장소는 Google의 공식 배포판이 아닙니다. Antigravity의 원본 바이너리나 코드를 포함·재배포하지 않으며, 사용자가 로컬에 설치한 `app.asar`에 런타임 한국어 번역 훅을 주입하는 스크립트와 번역 사전(`ko-dict.json`)만 제공합니다.

---

## 주요 특징

- **원클릭 적용 (별도 런타임 설치 불필요)**: Node.js가 없어도 Antigravity 내장 런타임(`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`)으로 바로 실행됩니다.
- **업데이트 자동 대응 런처**: 패치 시 생성되는 `Antigravity (한글)` 바로가기로 실행하면, Antigravity 업데이트로 `app.asar`가 초기화되었거나 `ko-dict.json`이 수정되었을 때만 자동으로 재패치 후 실행합니다. 평소에는 지연 없이 바로 열립니다.
- **코드·대화 내용 보호**: 코드 블록, 터미널, 에디터, 대화 본문 영역은 건드리지 않고 메뉴·설정·버튼·다이얼로그·툴팁 등 UI 요소만 번역합니다.
- **안전한 백업 및 즉시 원복**: 패치 전에 순정 `app.asar`를 `app.asar.bak`으로 자동 백업하고, 패치된 JS 문법(`vm.Script`)과 ASAR SHA-256 무결성 헤더를 검증한 뒤 반영합니다. `원본복구.cmd`로 언제든 순정 영문 상태로 되돌릴 수 있습니다.
- **쉬운 번역 수정·기여**: 모든 번역 문구가 `ko-dict.json` 파일 하나에 모여 있어 누구나 어색한 표현을 바로 고치거나 PR로 기여할 수 있습니다.

---

## 빠른 시작 (Windows)

### 1. 다운로드
- **Releases** 페이지에서 최신 `antigravity-ko-v*.zip` 파일을 내려받아 원하는 폴더(예: `C:\antigravity-ko`)에 압축을 풉니다.
- 또는 저장소를 클론합니다:
  ```powershell
  git clone https://github.com/pal815/antigravity-ko.git
  ```

### 2. 한글 패치 적용 및 실행
- **`한글패치-적용및실행.cmd`** 를 더블클릭합니다.
- 실행 중인 Antigravity가 안전하게 종료된 뒤, 한글 패치가 적용되어 자동으로 다시 열립니다.

### 3. 업데이트 후에도 한글화 유지하기 (권장)
- 패치 폴더에 생성된 **`Antigravity (한글)`** 바로가기를 사용하거나, **`바탕화면-바로가기-생성.cmd`** 를 실행해 바탕화면 아이콘으로 실행하세요.

Node.js가 설치되어 있다면 터미널에서도 직접 제어할 수 있습니다.

```powershell
node patch-agy.js --apply-and-launch        # 한글 패치 적용 및 실행
node patch-agy.js --smart-launch            # 업데이트/사전 변경 감지 시에만 재패치 후 실행
node patch-agy.js --status                  # 현재 패치 상태 및 사전 항목 수 확인

node patch-agy.js --restore                 # 순정 영문 상태로 복구
```

Antigravity를 기본 경로(`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Antigravity`)가 아닌 다른 위치에 설치한 경우 `ANTIGRAVITY_INSTALL_DIR` 환경 변수를 지정해 실행할 수 있습니다.

NFSCVita

Need for Speed Carbon, on the PS Vita

A fan port of the PC version of Need for Speed Carbon (2006, version 1.4)

Install  ·  Controls  ·  Settings  ·  Known issues  ·  Report a bug

> **Version 0.1.1, early pre-release.** Races, free roam and the career start (through the prologue into the free roam) work, but the game runs at about > 20 fps (target: 30) and there are known issues. Expect bugs; save often. > **Vibe-coded.** This port was written almost entirely by an AI coding assistant > ([Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)), directed and play-tested on a real Vita by the maintainer. Changes > are tested on hardware and logged in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md), but expect rough edges in the code. This is not a decompilation or a rewrite of the game. The code of your own `NFSC.exe` is translated to C++ ahead of time (static recompilation) and runs on the Vita with replacements for what the Vita lacks: Windows, Direct3D 9 (drawn with sceGxm), DirectSound, DirectInput and the Visual C++ 7.1 runtime. The gameplay itself (physics, AI, career, saves) is the game's own. **No game files are included.** You need your own copy of the PC game. The VPK contains the port's runtime and the code recompiled from the game's executable, but none of its data: the game reads that from your copy on the memory card. ## Requirements - Need for Speed Carbon for PC, **version 1.4**, installed (your own copy). The port is built against one exact `NFSC.exe` (unwrapped, 7,217,152 bytes, SHA-256 `baaaaec33873d4ba7e4dbae6a5212049ffdcf9679a35d865d7625b4189952fd3`), the same one the [Mac](https://github.com/vasist15-source/nfs-carbon-mac) and [Android](https://github.com/codepdbh/nfscarbonpc-androidevolved) ports require. # RustText

Текстовый редактор и просмотрщик больших логов для Windows x64 на Rust и GPUI Kit.

## Запуск

Для переносимой сборки распакуйте архив и запустите `rusttext.exe`. Отладочная и релизная сборки запускаются без отдельного окна консоли. Повторный запуск передаёт файлы открытому RustText. Сборка проверена на Windows 11 x64. Для Windows 10 x64 нужна отдельная проверка.

### Сборка из исходников

Нужны Rust с целью `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, инструменты C++ и Windows SDK из Visual Studio, а также CMake в `PATH`. Локальная сборка проверена с Rust 1.100.0 и CMake 4.5.0. Версия Rust закреплена в `rust-toolchain.toml`; Cargo по умолчанию собирает не более двух пакетов одновременно.

```powershell
cargo run --locked
cargo run --locked -- "C:\путь\к\файлу.txt"
```

- Верхнее меню содержит «Файл», «Инструменты» и «Поиск». Открытие и сохранение собраны в меню «Файл»; отдельной панели этих команд нет.
- Кнопка «+», двойной щелчок по свободному месту на полосе вкладок или `Ctrl+N` создают пустую вкладку. Пока вкладка не привязана к файлу, её заголовок повторяет первую строку текста в пределах настраиваемого лимита (по умолчанию 10 символов, для пустой строки – «Без имени»). «Файл → Открыть…» или `Ctrl+O` открывает файлы. Файлы также можно передать аргументами запуска или перетащить в окно.
- «Файл → Сохранить» (`Ctrl+S`) сохраняет документ, «Файл → Сохранить как…» (`Ctrl+Shift+S`) открывает диалог выбора пути. Для логов эти команды недоступны.
- Двойной щелчок по вкладке или `Ctrl+W` закрывает её. `Ctrl+Shift+T` или кнопка «↶» восстанавливают последнюю закрытую вкладку с её позицией и выделением в редакторе либо позицией и настройками просмотра лога. В меню «Файл → Закрытые вкладки» можно выбрать любую из последних 100 закрытых вкладок. История и текст вкладок «Без имени» сохраняются между запусками.
- Вкладки из сессии и закрытые черновики загружаются в фоне. Можно переключиться на другую вкладку или нажать «Отменить загрузку». Черновик остаётся в истории для повторного открытия. При восстановлении черновика размером свыше 8 МиБ, с более чем 50 000 строками или со строкой длиннее 64 КиБ RustText открывает постраничный просмотр. «Сохранить копию…» выгружает весь черновик в UTF-8.
- Нижняя строка состояния показывает путь или уведомление, состояние сохранения документа, позицию курсора (`Ctrl+G` открывает переход к строке), кодировку и переводы строк.
- «Файл → Недавние файлы» показывает 16 последних открытых или сохранённых файлов. После закрытия всех вкладок либо по нажатию на «RustText» в левом верхнем углу открывается полная история с поиском и страницами. В истории и меню «Недавние файлы» и «Закрытые вкладки» отображаются доступные количество строк и время последней работы. За последние сутки время указано в минутах или часах, для более старых записей показаны местные дата и время. На открытой странице истории относительное время обновляется автоматически. Если есть записи младше часа, обновления происходят не чаще раза в 10 секунд, а если остались…

# @shapeshift-labs/ink-studio

A JavaScript toolkit for sculpting signed-distance solids, baking them into pixel-art Gaussian splats, and making them move, react, break, grow and remember what happened to them. Use it from Node, drive it through the `ink-studio` command, or embed the source bundle in an Inkwell or browser application.

The package includes geometry, materials, lighting, animation, character controls, particles, physics, procedural generation, and retained authoring. Write scenes in JavaScript or JSON, render images through the CPU-based Node and CLI tools, or draw into a canvas with the default WebGL 2 browser renderer. Browser hosts supply the editor UI and advance the scene.

## Contents

- [Install and run](#install-and-run)
- [First sculpted scene](#first-sculpted-scene)
- [Using the library in Node](#using-the-library-in-node)

- [View-dependent surface materials](#view-dependent-surface-materials)
- [Projected and procedural effects](#projected-and-procedural-effects)
- [Reflections, ripples and atmosphere](#reflections-ripples-and-atmosphere)
- [Embedding and custom scene collections](#embedding-and-custom-scene-collections)
- [Browser renderer](#browser-renderer)
- [Screen transitions](#screen-transitions)
- [Module reference](#module-reference)
- [Validation and development](#validation-and-development)

## Install and run

Requires **Node 18 or later**. There are no declared runtime dependencies. The package is available from GitHub.

From a checkout:

```sh
node cli/ink-studio.js help
node cli/ink-studio.js scenes
node cli/ink-studio.js render watcher --t 2.6
node cli/ink-studio.js render watcher --t 2.6 --colored
npm test
```

Install from GitHub:

```sh
npm install github:siliconjungle/shapeshift-labs-ink-studio
npx ink-studio help
```

To install a local checkout into another project:

```sh
npm install /absolute/path/to/ink-studio
npx ink-studio help
npx ink-studio render watcher --colored
```

The installed package is named `@shapeshift-labs/ink-studio`, and its executable is `ink-studio`. The `private` setting prevents accidental registry publication.

Generated pictures normally go into `studio/out/`. Image baselines go into `studio/snaps/`. Use `--out file.png` for an explicit output path, or configure the directories with `ink-studio.config.js`.

# ScanDot

[![CI](https://github.com/faizfahmi77/ScanDot/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/faizfahmi77/ScanDot/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

ScanDot is an experimental Android app for capturing and viewing 3D point clouds on a supported phone. It combines ARCore camera tracking and depth estimates, saves scans locally, and provides an interactive viewer.

The repository also contains a separate video photogrammetry pipeline that runs on a workstation using FFmpeg and COLMAP. **The Android app does not reconstruct ordinary video with photogrammetry on the phone.**

## Current status

- Capture, save and reopen point clouds on devices that support ARCore Depth.
- Rotate, pan and zoom scans in the viewer. An optional full-depth mode interpolates missing depth and can distort surfaces.
- Prepare video frames and run a sparse or dense COLMAP reconstruction on a workstation.

This is an early prototype. Results can contain gaps, drift and noise; they are not textured meshes or validated measurements. Reflective, transparent and textureless subjects are difficult. Capture quality and device compatibility need further testing.

## Try the preview

Download the [preview APK](https://github.com/faizfahmi77/ScanDot/releases/tag/v0.3.0-preview.1). The release notes describe compatibility and signing limitations.

## Build the Android app

You need JDK 17, Android SDK 36, and an Android device with ARCore Depth support. Camera permission is required; Google Play Services for AR may require installation or an update.

```sh
cd android-app
./gradlew assembleDebug lintDebug testDebugUnitTest
```

On Windows, use `gradlew.bat` in place of `./gradlew`. The debug APK is written to `android-app/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`. Install it as an update to preserve existing app data.

In the app, name the scan, tap **Start scan**, and move slowly around the subject in good light. Save it, then open it from **Results**. Scans are stored in the app's private storage; uninstalling the app removes them.

## Workstation video pipeline

The benchmark requires Python 3.12 or newer, FFmpeg, FFprobe and a compatible COLMAP installation. Dense reconstruction requires a compatible COLMAP configuration. From the repository root:

```sh
python -m processing.benchmark prepare "path/to/input.mp4" --output "path/to/new-run" --fps 5
python -m processing.benchmark reconstruct "path/to/new-run" --colmap "path/to/colmap" --dense
```

The output directory must not already exist. Omit `--dense` for a sparse-only run. See the subcommand `--help` output for options. A successful run does not establish complete or accurate geometry.

The Python tests use the standard library:

```sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## Project structure

```text
android-app/  Android capture, local storage and point-cloud viewer
processing/   Video preparation and COLMAP orchestration
tests/        Python tests with synthetic fixtures
tools/        Workstation utilities…

quer3q/kraken-mount.content: A PS5 game mounter. It finds games on the internal SSD, the M.2 drive and USB drives. **Supported formats**: debug FPKG (`.pkg`) and game folders (plain, or packed with zstd or LZ4). For large, demanding games, use the zstd pack format: it performs better than FPKG. ## How to 1. Download `kraken-mount.elf` from [Releases](https://github.com/quer3q/kraken-mount/releases) and send it to your jailbroken PS5 with the ELF loader (elfldr, port 9021) or payload-manager: `nc -w 3 9021 < kraken-mount.elf`. kstuff must be loaded, and ShadowMount+ must not be running: Kraken Mount waits until both are true. 2. Put each game in a scan root: - internal SSD: `/data/homebrew`, `/data/etaHEN/games` - M.2 or extended drive (`/mnt/ext0`, `/mnt/ext1`): `homebrew`, `etaHEN/games` or the drive root - USB drive (`/mnt/usb0` to `/mnt/usb7`): `homebrew`, `etaHEN/games` or the drive root 3. Each game gets a " registered" notification and its own home-screen tile. [ampr-emu-ng](https://github.com/quer3q/ampr-emu-ng) comes bundled and is installed into `/data/krakenmount/ampr/` at start. To run another build, put its `libSceAmpr.sprx` there; it is kept until you delete it. A game that needs the DLC or PlayGo emulator and ships none gets the bundled one in its fakelib (setting `add_emulators`, on by default); a game's own copy is kept, unless it is a known older release of the bundled one, which is upgraded. Details: [DLC emulator](docs/dlcemu.md), [PlayGo stub](docs/playgo.md). Caches live in `/data/krakenmount/caches/`, settings in `/data/krakenmount/config.toml` and the log in `/data/krakenmount/kraken.log`. To build it yourself: `ps5/build.sh` (needs Docker), output `target/ps5/kraken-mount.elf`. ## Thanks - [drakmor/ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus): home-screen registration, the fakelib sandbox overlay and backports are ported from it. - [drakmor/dlc_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/dlc_emu): the bundled DLC emulator (`libSceAppContent.sprx`, `libSceNpEntitlementAccess.sprx`, `libSceGameUpdate.sprx`), added to a game's fakelib when the game has a `dlc_emu.ini` at its root; a known older release the game ships is upgraded, any other copy is kept. - [drakmor/pgo_stub](https://github.com/drakmor/pgo_stub): the bundled PlayGo stub (`libScePlayGo.sprx`), added to a game's fakelib when its `eboot.bin` imports `libScePlayGo` and the game ships none. - [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk): the PS5 toolchain. ## License GPL-3.0-or-later (`LICENSE`). Third-party notices are in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`.

## 界面速览

     

## 功能 | 功能 | 可以看到或做到什么 | | --- | --- | | 行为记录 | 按时间、应用或类型查看位置、剪贴板、设备标识等 **12 类数据、56 种访问**，也可以筛选后台记录。 | | 需要关注 | 集中查看后台发送数据、后台读取敏感数据、短时间内频繁访问和反复被拒的尝试。 | | 网络活动 | 按应用查看连接地址和可用的流量统计。开启域名记录后，可显示关联到的域名。 | | 系统历史 | 在应用详情查看 Android 保留的权限访问明细和累计次数，包括开始监测前的部分行为。 | | 日志导出 | 在「设置 › 导出日志」将选定时段的记录导出为包含 CSV 的 ZIP，供保存和分析。 | | 通知 | 监测时常驻一条精简通知，显示已监测时长并带停止按钮，可在「设置 › 通知」关闭。可选显示这次监测的应用数和记录数；开启「需要关注提醒」后，应用新出现需要关注的行为时会通知你，同一次监测里同一应用的同一项只提醒一次。 | ## 管理应用 「应用」页按来源整理应用。在应用详情里查看行为记录，再决定要不要改动。所有管理操作都由你发起，揪咪改动后会读回系统状态确认是否生效，系统拒绝时显示原因。

   

| 操作 | 会发生什么 | | --- | --- | | 权限管理 | 在应用详情的「权限管理」里逐项关闭或开启权限。「可控权限总开关」一次关闭全部，再打开时只恢复揪咪关闭过的权限。系统锁定的权限标为只读。 | | 联网管理 | 在支持的设备上，通过 Android 自带的防火墙为单个应用关闭或恢复联网，不占用 VPN。应用与其他应用共用 UID、规则由其他工具设置，或无法确认只影响这一个应用时，开关会锁定并说明原因。 | | 冻结与解冻 | 冻结会让 Android 为当前用户停用这个应用并保留数据，可在「应用 › 已冻结」解冻。已冻结的应用图标带雪花标记。 | | 冻结失效 | 揪咪冻结过的应用如果又被启用，列表和详情会标为「冻结已失效」，时间线记下发现的时间；无法得知是谁启用的。开启「设置 › 应用管理 › 冻结失效时自动重新冻结」后，会再冻结一次。 | | 删除自己安装的应用 | 输入完整包名确认后，揪咪先备份安装包再卸载。之后可在「应用 › 已删除」尝试装回。**应用数据会随卸载删除，备份只能恢复安装包。** | | 移除预装应用 | 在「设置 › 应用管理」开启后，可为当前用户移除受支持的预装应用。系统中的原件和应用数据会保留，可在「应用 › 已删除」尝试恢复。 | 「设置 › 应用管理」的「执行身份」显示这些操作以谁的身份执行。使用 Root，或以 Root 启动的 Shizuku 时，冻结、解冻、为当前用户删除和恢复以 Root 身份执行，能更改手机不允许 shell 更改的系统应用；使用无线调试时以 shell 身份执行，部分系统应用手机不允许更改，揪咪会说明原因。卸载自己安装的应用只影响当前用户，工作资料或分身里的同一应用会保留。 核心系统组件默认受保护。改动手机依赖的组件可能影响系统功能，揪咪会在操作前提示风险。 ## 不用 Root，怎么看到后台？ Android 在应用运行时会产生权限访问记录、连接表、系统跟踪和事件日志。揪咪探针以 **shell 身份**读取可用的系统信号，App 再按规则整理成记录，存入手机上的数据库。监测过程不会向其他应用注入代码。冻结、删除、关闭权限和联网等操作需要你在应用管理中主动发起。

Please report what you find. ## Two modes, one switch The big **Simple / Advanced** switch in the header decides what is tested. The route diagram under the title morphs to show it. | | **Simple** | **Advanced** | |---|---|---| | Question it answers | *Which of my configs work?* | *Which free configs work through my config?* | | Route | you → **config** → AI Studio / Gemini | you → **base config** → **free config** → AI Studio / Gemini | | You provide | your configs (links, a subscription URL or base64), or pick a ready-made free list | one working base config, plus a free list or pasted configs | | Anti-DPI profile is applied to | every config under test (each one connects from your machine) | the base config's first hop (free configs run inside its tunnel) | | Typical use | check a pile of configs you already have; test a config before you rely on it | your Cloudflare config works, but you need a *different exit* that Google accepts | | Export | links, base64, a full Xray config of one config | links, base64, a chain Xray config (`base → free`) | ## Contents [Credits](#credits-and-references) · [Why a signed-in browser](#why-a-signed-in-browser) · [Download and install](#download-and-install) · [User guide](#user-guide) · [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting-and-faq) · [Privacy and security](#privacy-and-security) · [Build from source](#build-from-source) · [Releases and CI](#releases-and-ci) ## Credits and references This project exists because of other people's work.
